title: The Last Lamp Across the Saltglass

nodes.brief: Opening: the reader is a runner of the Ember-Lamp Post at Candlemere on the western rim of the dried Saltglass Basin; the town's harvest has failed and the elders hand over the Seedkey. The monsoon (the Return) will flood the basin in twenty days.

exits.label: Clasp the ceramic rod without speaking a word

exits.intent: Ask the elders what they are not saying
exits.label: Demand to know why previous runners never returned

nodes.title: The Ember Lamp Post
nodes.page:
Dust hangs thick in the low-beamed hall of the Ember-Lamp Post, where the elders of Candlemere gather around a dead hearth. The valley harvests have shrivelled into grey ash, and the twenty-day countdown to the monsoon has begun. Across the splintered oak table lies a cold ceramic rod, smooth and pale as bone. The oldest councillor pushes it toward you, her fingers trembling with the chill of a failing town.

You must carry this to the centre of the dried Basin before the Return drowns everything you love.

nodes.brief: The reader takes the Seedkey straight from the elder's hand; describe the key (a cold ceramic key as long as a hand) and what it opens (the Rain Vault of Prism, the last drought-proof seed hall).

exits.intent: Go to pack for the road
exits.label: Turn away from the empty hearth and prepare your pack

nodes.title: Weight of the Seedkey
nodes.page: Your fingers close around the Seedkey, and ceramic chill bites straight through your palm. As long as a hand and shaped like a closed pod, it is the only thing standing between Candlemere and absolute hunger. This cold key alone can turn the ancient bronze locks of the Rain Vault deep beneath Prism, the observatory-city at the heart of the Saltglass Basin, where the final drought-proof seeds lie sleeping.

nodes.brief: The reader questions the elders; they admit nobody has come back from Prism in twelve years and the Salt Court has been buying every well. Include the description of the Seedkey and the Rain Vault.

exits.intent: Go to pack for the road
exits.label: Sling your provisions over your shoulder and prepare for the journey

nodes.title: Shadows of the Past
nodes.page: Silence settles over the low-beamed hall as your question hangs in the dry air. The eldest councillor trades a long look with the others before admitting that no runner has returned from Prism in twelve long years, while the predatory Salt Court has bought up every remaining water well on the rim. Yet the ceramic Seedkey remains your only hope - a cold, hand-sized rod capable of unlocking the Rain Vault beneath Prism and saving the valley from the coming drought.

nodes.brief: Packing at dawn at the Lamp-Post; the reader's family or friends see them off; the ember-lamp, a water skin and the Rim Road ahead.

exits.intent: Step out onto the Rim Road
exits.label: Step out onto the dusty track of the Rim Road

nodes.title: Dawn on the Rim
nodes.page: Dawn breaks hard and white over the western rim of the Saltglass Basin, casting long shadows across the dry dust of Candlemere. Your neighbours stand in quiet clusters by the paddock fence, watching you secure the leather water-skin and bank the glowing coals within your tin lantern. The horizon stretches out like a sheet of hammered tin, blinding in the early glare.

nodes.brief: Arrival in Candlemere and the Rim Road: the lamp-town on the western rim, outfitting, rivals and kin, the first miles of the Rim Road; the reader hires help and takes the ember-lamp. The reader enters with several ways forward.

exits.label: Follow the winding lamp-lit track ahead
Step off the stones onto the open common ground

exits.intent: Ask the way of a stranger
exits.label: Hail a weathered traveller for directions
Take the steep and stony drovers' track

nodes.title: The Rim Road
nodes.page: Candlemere hums with the desperate energy of a dying town as you step onto the sun-bleached gravel of the Rim Road. Outfitting stalls spill over with dried salt-meat and copper canteens, while rival runners and anxious kin eye your preparations with wary curiosity. You check the banked coals of your ember-lamp and adjust the strap of your pack, feeling the vast, silent glare of the Basin waiting just beyond the ridge.

nodes.brief: Mandatory scene at the Lamp-Post Gate: the reader decides whether to hire the glass-diver Calder, a wry guide who knows the Saltglass, or go alone

exits.intent: Hire Calder the glass-diver as guide
exits.label: Hire Calder the glass-diver as guide to lead the way across the white flats

exits.intent: Go alone, trusting your own feet
exits.label: Go alone, trusting your own feet to navigate the perilous basin.

nodes.title: The Diver's Offer
nodes.page:
The heavy timber gates of Candlemere stand wide behind you, framing the vast, blinding expanse of the Saltglass Basin where your journey truly begins. Calder lingers by the stone post, his brass sounding-lead swinging in a slow, hypnotic arc as he waits to see whether you intend to face the treacherous salt-crust alone or secure his seasoned company. Every traveller who has crossed these flats warns of hidden sinkholes and deceptive mirages, making the choice of companionship a matter of survival before the monsoon twenty days away.

You feel the reassuring cold weight of the Seedkey resting in your travelling pack, reminding you that failure is not an option for the parched lamp-town of Candlemere.

nodes.brief: Mandatory scene at the Last Lamp-Stall: the reader decides whether to light the ember-lamp (it draws attention and warms the night) or carry it banked dark

exits.intent: Light the ember-lamp and carry it
exits.label: Light the wick to guide your step through the dark

exits.intent: Bank the lamp dark in its case to save oil
exits.label: Bank the lamp tight inside its iron housing for stealth

nodes.title: The Lamp-Stall Choice
nodes.page: Thick tallow smoke curls around the wooden beams of the Last Lamp-Stall as you weigh your departure. To blaze your path with the lamp's exposed flame invites every eye across the basin, yet keeps the bitter night chill at bay. Alternatively, banking the lantern deep within its case preserves your precious oil and cloaks your passage in secrecy, leaving you to feel your way blindly through the rising wind.

nodes.brief: Leaving Candlemere and the Rim Road for The Bitterflats: close this part of the journey.

exits.label: Proceed deeper into the shimmering desert

nodes.title: Leaving the Rim Road
nodes.page:
Candlemere and the familiar safety of the Rim Road fall entirely behind you as you cross the threshold into the great white expanse of the Bitterflats. Every familiar landmark disappears into the vibrating heat haze, leaving only the endless salt crust and the distant gleam of the glass cities. You check your provisions and ensure your ember-lamp is secure, knowing that turning back is no longer an option.

The vast journey toward the centre of the Basin has truly begun.

nodes.brief: In the tallow-smelling vault of the Ember-Lamp Post, your aunt presses the cold ceramic Seedkey into your palm with a sharp warning about the looming monsoon.

exits.label: Push past the heavy hide curtain toward the yard
Trade for a sturdy mule near the boiling pitch-pots
Accept a cracked whetstone under the tavern sign

nodes.title: The Tallow Vault
nodes.page: In the tallow-smelling vault of the Ember-Lamp Post, your aunt presses the cold ceramic Seedkey into your palm with a sharp warning about the looming monsoon. The air is heavy with rendered fat and old smoke, clinging to your woolens like a second skin. Outside, the white expanse of the Saltglass Basin bakes beneath a pitiless sky, giving you twenty days to cross the dead sea before the rains wipe the tracks clean forever.

nodes.brief: Behind the curtain of beaded sheep gut in the tallow-loft, your cousin Garrow thrusts a smouldering coal-lantern into your grip while cursing the dry wells of Candlemere.

exits.label: Step through the narrow alleyway behind the cooperage
Slip the lucky copper button into your pocket
Seek reassurance near the dying public bakehouse

nodes.title: The Tallow-Loft
nodes.page: Behind the curtain of beaded sheep gut in the tallow-loft, your cousin Garrow thrusts a smouldering coal-lantern into your grip while cursing the dry wells of Candlemere. Yellow smoke makes your eyes water as you secure the lantern to your belt, and banked heat settles against your thigh. The town around you is packing its remaining treasures, bracing for the inevitable march of the bitter drought.

nodes.brief: Upon the salt-crusted limestone steps of the Grand Cistern, the village elder hands you a water-skin that tastes of iron and entrusts you with the survival of the valley.

exits.label: Inquire about the Glasswright signals at the bakehouse
Acquire a vial of bitter willow oil from the apothecary
Accept the greasy wool blanket by the sheep-pens

nodes.title: The Grand Cistern
nodes.page: Upon the salt-crusted limestone steps of the Grand Cistern, the village elder hands you a water-skin that tastes of iron and entrusts you with the survival of the valley. The stone basin below is cracked and bone-dry, echoing with the hollow sound of your own boots. Every household has contributed a drop from their dwindling reserves to fill your flask for the long trek across the Basin.

nodes.brief: Inside the low-roofed tannery where the grease vats steam, your uncle ties the leather harness across your chest and reminds you that twenty days remain before the Basin drowns.

exits.label: Measure your stride past the watchful debt-collector
Accept the smooth pebble from the weeping child

nodes.title: The Tannery Floor
nodes.page: Inside the low-roofed tannery where the grease vats steam, your uncle ties the leather harness across your chest and reminds you that twenty days remain before the Basin drowns. The pungent smell of oak bark and lime fills the damp air, sticking to the back of your throat. He pats your shoulder with a hand hardened by decades of scraping hides, wishing you safe passage through the glass cities.

nodes.brief: Beneath the copper eaves of the south granary, a Salt Court bailiff blocks your path to weigh your pack and demand an exorbitant toll for the Rim Road.

exits.label: Speak with the grey-wool robed Dune Sister
Join the carters debating the southern route
Sharpen your skinning knife beside the wagon

nodes.title: The South Granary
nodes.page: Beneath the copper eaves of the south granary, a Salt Court bailiff blocks your path to weigh your pack and demand an exorbitant toll for the Rim Road. The bailiff's polished brass scales gleam mockingly in the harsh morning light, reflecting the desperate desperation of every runner heading toward the interior. The air tastes of dry salt and rising heat.

nodes.brief: Beside the boiling pitch-pots of the upper square, an anxious tanner tries to trade his spare mule for a share of whatever rain-seed you might bring back from Prism.

exits.label: Lead the skinny mule down toward the cart-tracks.
Refuse the beast and walk past the boiling vats alone.

nodes.title: The Pitch-Pots
nodes.page: Thick black smoke drifts from the boiling pitch-pots of the upper square, smelling of hot resin and sulfur. Beside the bubbling vats, a grease-stained tanner wipes his brow and tries to trade his spare mule for a share of whatever rain-seed you might bring back from Prism. He swears the beast is sure-footed over white crust, though its ribs look like barrel hoops under the harsh daylight. You touch the cold ceramic key hidden in your vest and weigh his desperate offer against the heavy miles waiting beyond the rim.

nodes.brief: Under the creaking sign of the Blind Owl tavern, a desperate barley-grower presses a cracked whetstone into your pocket in exchange for a promise of future irrigation.

exits.label: Accept the stone and head toward the old milestone.
Leave the whetstone on the lintel and climb the gravel ledge.
Turn back toward the terrace mounting block to check your pack.

nodes.title: The Blind Owl
nodes.page: Under the creaking wooden sign of the Blind Owl tavern, the morning air tastes of baked dust and old beer lees. A desperate barley-grower intercepts you near the lintel, pressing a cracked stone whetstone into your pocket with trembling fingers in exchange for a solemn promise of future irrigation when the vault opens. His fields are cracked plates of grey mud, and his eyes hold the hollow look of men who have watched their wells turn to brine.

nodes.brief: Within the narrow stone alley behind the cooperage, an old woman named Morwen thrusts a pouch of dried mint leaves against the dust cough that waits on the salt flats.

exits.label: Step past her out onto the gravel ledge overlooking the white Basin.
Follow the steep alley toward the stone mounting block by the terrace edge.
Veer toward the rotting canvas awning where the prospector sits.

nodes.title: The Cooperage Alley
nodes.page: Deep in the narrow stone alley behind the cooperage, the shade offers little relief from the furnace glare of the sky. An old woman named Morwen catches your sleeve, thrusting a coarse linen pouch of dried mint leaves against your chest to ward off the dry dust cough that waits on the open salt flats. She mutters ancient cautions about the dry wind while her spotted fingers trace the leather harness over your ribs. The passage opens ahead into brighter light, splitting toward the rim and the high ledges.

nodes.brief: At the communal washing troughs where the grey silt settles, your younger sister slips a lucky copper button into your collar lining to keep the dry wind from freezing your lungs.

exits.label: Walk past the fluttering wool rags on the dead acacia tree.
Take the upper track where the path splits into jagged limestone ribs.

nodes.title: The Washing Troughs
nodes.page: At the communal washing troughs where the grey silt settles into dry crusts, the water is long gone and only salt-rings remain on the stone. Your younger sister waits by the deepest basin, slipping a lucky copper button into your collar lining to keep the dry wind from freezing your lungs on the march. Her hands are cold despite the heat, and her smile is too thin for comfort. The track leads away from the familiar stone walls toward the open desert and the distant, shimmering ruins of the old lensfolk.

nodes.brief: Near the public bakehouse where the hearths are dying, a nervous baker begs you to confirm whether the Glasswrights of Prism are still sending mirror signals across the Basin.

exits.label: Head toward the stone mounting block at the edge of the terrace.
Make your way toward the rotting canvas awning near the old bakehouse wall.

nodes.title: The Public Bakehouse
nodes.page: Near the public bakehouse where the hearths have been cold for weeks, a nervous baker grabs your arm and begs you to confirm whether the Glasswrights of Prism are still sending mirror signals across the Basin. His flour bins are empty, and he fears the sky-watchers have abandoned their posts in the glass towers. You look across the white expanse where the mirages dance before answering him. The road stretches out below, demanding a choice between the lower mule tracks and the rough terrace paths.

nodes.brief: Across the threshold of the apothecary stall, a sharp-eyed herbalist offers you a vial of bitter willow oil if you promise to scout for her missing brother near the old wharves.

exits.label: Take the upper track toward the limestone ribs.
Choose the dry irrigation channel choked with tumbleweed.
Climb to the dusty platform of the disused relay station.

nodes.title: The Apothecary Stall
nodes.page: Across the threshold of the apothecary stall, shelves of dried roots and sealed earthen jars rattle in the rising draft. A sharp-eyed herbalist offers you a small vial of bitter willow oil if you promise to scout for her missing brother near the old wharves where the salt crust thickens. She holds the glass up to the light to show its clear amber depth before corking it tight with red wax. The path outside divides among the ruins, offering three distinct ways down toward the edge of the dried sea.

nodes.brief: Behind the timber stockade where the sheep-pens stand empty, a weary herdsman hands you a greasy wool blanket and warns you that the desert nights are as sharp as broken glass.

exits.label: Take the lower track toward the stone huts
Follow the wagon ruts past the empty trough

nodes.title: The Empty Sheep Pens
nodes.page: Behind the timber stockade where the sheep-pens stand empty, a weary herdsman hands you a greasy wool blanket and warns you that the desert nights are as sharp as broken glass. The wind whistling through the dry cedar poles carries the cold bite of the distant salt flats, reminding you that your wool coat alone will not hold out the frost. He gestures toward two different paths winding away from the pens into the gathering dusk, advising you to seek shelter before the shadows lengthen across the dust.

nodes.brief: In the shadows of the salt-warehouse porch, a debt-collector from the valley below measures your stride with greedy eyes and calculates how much your boots will fetch at auction.

exits.label: Walk past the old signalman polishing his brass mirror disc.
Pass the dry stone drinking trough where the mule handler packs his gear.

nodes.title: The Salt-Warehouse Porch
nodes.page: In the deep shadows of the salt-warehouse porch, a debt-collector from the valley below measures your stride with greedy eyes and calculates how much your sturdy boots will fetch at auction if you fail to return. He taps a brass ledger against his knee and remarks that many runners start this journey with lighter packs than yours. The road lies open before you, running past the old relay station and down toward the grey drinking troughs where the last livestock was watered.

nodes.brief: By the public well whose iron handle hangs slack and dry, a weeping child presses a smooth pebble into your hand and asks if the rain is truly coming back this year.

exits.label: Pick your way toward the roofless shell of the old storage hut.
Head for the stone drinking trough where the mule handler prepares to leave.

nodes.title: The Public Well
nodes.page: By the public well whose iron handle hangs slack and dry against the stonework, a weeping child presses a smooth river pebble into your hand and asks if the rain is truly coming back this year. The wooden bucket rests at the bottom of the empty shaft, kicking up a hollow echo when the wind blows across the rim. You close your fist around the cool stone and step away from the curb, facing the long road that winds down into the white glare of the Basin.

nodes.brief: Past the outer drying racks where white fish-skins stiffen in the glare, a Dune Sister in grey wool offers you a cup of brackish well-water in exchange for a binding oath of silence.

exits.label: Follow the white rim-track where the wind hums through fence wire.

nodes.title: The Outer Drying Racks
nodes.page: Past the outer drying racks where white fish-skins stiffen in the glare, a Dune Sister wrapped in coarse grey wool blocks your path. She offers you a cup of brackish well-water from a skin flask in exchange for a binding oath of silence regarding the hidden desert wells. Her eyes are pale as salt crystals, and her fingers do not release the leather strap until you give your word. The white road stretches away from the racks, humming with the dry vibration of the Rim.

nodes.brief: At the crossroads where the cart-tracks sink into white crust, a group of idle carters debate whether the southern mirror-posts have been smashed by salt-storms or desert thieves.

exits.label: Inspect the jagged glass cliff ahead
Investigate the rusted ore-crusher in the dust

nodes.title: The Crossroads Debate
nodes.page: Iron-bound cart-tracks cut deep into white salt crust where idlers gather in the glare. Three dust-caked carters lean against a wooden axle, arguing fiercely over whether the southern mirror-posts have been smashed by salt-storms or looted by desert thieves. You adjust the heavy strap of your ember-lamp, feeling the warmth of its banked coals against your hip while the cold ceramic weight of the Seedkey taps your ribs through your tunic. The open basin stretches ahead, white and blinding under the midday sun.

nodes.brief: Under the skeletal ribs of an old timber wagon, a traveling tinker sharpens a skinning knife on a flat river stone and mutters dark tales about the singing hollows of the lower flats.

exits.label: Avoid the hollows near the old watch-cabins
Watch the mirror-guild apprentice practice on the shelf

nodes.title: The Tinker's Knife
nodes.page:
Beneath the skeletal ribs of an abandoned timber wagon, a traveling tinker sits cross-legged and sharpens a narrow skinning knife against a flat river stone with a rhythmic rasp. He pauses to spit into the dust, muttering dark tales about the singing hollows of the lower flats where the wind plays strange tunes through the shattered glass streets. Your ember-lamp casts a faint heat against your thigh, a reminder of the twenty days left before the monsoon floods the basin.

Choose to heed the tinker's warning and take the upper trail or descend directly toward the low ruins.

nodes.brief: Beside a crumbling limestone marker post, an old shepherd warns you that the salt haze rising from the dead floor can twist a runner's wits before noon if the lamp isn't trimmed.

exits.label: Pass quietly by the abandoned watch-cabins
Approach the solitary fire by the old crusher

nodes.title: The Shepherd's Warning
nodes.page: A crumbling limestone marker post leans drunkenly beside the track, and an old shepherd stands near it, shading his rheumy eyes against the glare. He warns you that the salt haze rising from the dead floor can twist a runner's wits before noon if the ember-lamp isn't properly trimmed and tended. You check the small air vent on the lantern, smelling the familiar, comforting scent of banked coal and dried peat.

nodes.brief: On the gravel ledge overlooking the white expanse of the Basin, a lone sentinel peers through a cracked brass spyglass at the distant, glittering towers of Prism.

exits.label: Walk down toward the smoke in the dust
Watch the mirror-guild apprentice flash the signals

nodes.title: The Distant Towers
nodes.page: A lone sentinel stands upon a gravel ledge overlooking the immense, shimmering expanse of the Basin, peering intently through a cracked brass spyglass at the distant, glittering towers of Prism. The observatory-city catches the light like a cluster of jagged diamonds embedded in the white salt crust. Your fingers brush the cold ceramic Seedkey tucked securely inside your coat, anchoring you against the immense emptiness of the dead sea.

nodes.brief: Near the stone mounting block at the edge of the terrace, a mule-teamer counts his remaining fodder bags and curses the day he signed away his water rights to the Salt Court.

exits.label: Approach the solitary fire in the white dust
Observe the mirror-guild apprentice on the limestone shelf
Follow the stray dog past the traveler's cairn

nodes.title: The Mule-Teamer's Curse
nodes.page:
Near the stone mounting block at the edge of the terrace, a sweating mule-teamer counts his remaining fodder bags and curses the day he signed away his water rights to the Salt Court. His animals stamp restlessly in the fine white dust, their ribs showing sharp beneath dusty hides. You keep your distance, gripping the iron handle of your ember-lamp as you weigh the paths stretching out before you across the blistering rim road.

Choose to walk toward the solitary fire, watch the mirror-guild apprentice, or follow the stray dog down the ridge.

nodes.brief: Beside a dead acacia tree hung with fluttering wool rags, an itinerant ballad-singer chants a mournful verse about the drowned kings who sleep beneath the glass streets.

exits.label: Watch the mirror-guild apprentice practice flash signals
Inspect the broken lintel of the customs post

nodes.title: The Ballad-Singer's Verse
nodes.page: A dead acacia tree hangs heavy with fluttering wool rags that snap dryly in the hot wind, casting jagged shadows over the gravel. Beside the trunk, an itinerant ballad-singer chants a mournful, nasal verse about the drowned kings who sleep beneath the glass streets of the old empire. The haunting melody lingers in the dry air long after you step past him, your ember-lamp swaying gently with your stride.

nodes.brief: Under the shade of a rotting canvas awning, a dusty prospector cleans red salt out of his eyeteeth and tries to sell you a worthless chunk of pyrite as a navigation talisman.

exits.label: Descend the steep goat path to the salt-crust
Seek shelter near the wind-scoured limestone arch
Climb the high gravel ridge where the old axle lies

nodes.title: The Prospector's Pyrite
nodes.page:
Under the shade of a rotting canvas awning that flaps in the hot draft, a dusty prospector cleans red salt out of his eyeteeth with a bone splinter. He holds up a worthless chunk of yellow pyrite, trying to sell it to you as a navigation talisman for the glass mazes. You shake your head, keeping your hand firmly on the warm casing of your ember-lamp as you look out over the diverging tracks.

Choose to descend the goat path toward the salt-crust, seek shelter near the wind-scoured arch, or climb the high gravel ridge.

nodes.brief: At the junction where the upper track splits into jagged limestone ribs, a nervous courier from the west demands to know if the mountain passes are still choked with red shale.

exits.label: Inspect the broken lintel of the customs post
Visit the lonely hermit by the sulfurous mud-pot

nodes.title: The Nervous Courier
nodes.page: At the junction where the upper track splits into jagged limestone ribs, a nervous courier from the west halts his panting mule and demands to know if the mountain passes are still choked with red shale. His eyes dart toward the blinding white expanse of the Basin as if expecting pursuit from the Salt Court toll-lords. You offer a noncommittal nod, shifting the weight of the Seedkey against your chest before choosing your footing on the fractured stone.

nodes.brief: Beside a dry irrigation channel choked with tumbleweed, a lonely ditcher offers to share his roasted lizard meat if you will tell him the latest news from the valley capital.

exits.label: Descend the steep goat path to the salt-crust
Visit the lonely hermit by the sulfurous mud-pot
Approach the displaced herders near the limestone arch

nodes.title: The Ditcher's Share
nodes.page:
Beside a dry irrigation channel choked with pale tumbleweed, a lonely ditcher sits in the meager shade of a dirt bank, roasting a strip of tough lizard meat over a tiny flame. He offers to share his meager meal if you will pause to tell him the latest news from the valley capital and whether the rains are truly coming. You adjust your coat against the glare, feeling the banked lantern warm your side as you weigh the paths ahead.

Choose to descend the goat path, visit the sulfurous mud-pot, or approach the limestone arch.

nodes.brief: Within the roofless shell of an old storage hut, a weary scout patches his split boot-soles with copper wire and warns you that the northern sinkholes are widening.

exits.label: Follow the high gravel ridge across the slope
Walk past the dry sinkhole with the mule skeleton

nodes.title: The Scout's Warning
nodes.page: Within the roofless shell of an old storage hut built from sun-baked mud bricks, a weary scout patches his split boot-soles with stiff copper wire. He looks up without smiling, warning you that the northern sinkholes are widening under the heat and the salt crust is dangerously thin in the lower hollows. You thank him quietly, patting the metal casing of your ember-lamp to ensure the coals are still banked and safe for the long road ahead.

nodes.brief: On the dusty platform of the disused relay station, an old signalman polishes a brass mirror disc while watching for the morning flash from the Glasswrights' towers.

exits.label: Follow the path toward the limestone arch
Descend toward the cliff overhang

nodes.title: The Signalman's Mirror
nodes.page:
Dust spirals skip across the platform of the disused relay station while an old signalman polishes a brass mirror disc with the hem of his faded tunic. He pauses every few seconds to squint toward the distant towers of Prism, searching the blinding morning glare for any answering flash from the Glasswrights. Your ember-lamp rests at your hip, banked coals warming your thigh through the cloth. The signalman glances your way, offering a toothless grin and a nod toward the winding tracks ahead.

You can press onward past the relay station toward the distant limestone arch, or turn your steps along the low ridge toward the orange-stained cliff.

nodes.brief: By the stone drinking trough where the green algae has turned to grey dust, a frightened mule handler packs up his empty crates and turns his beasts back toward the town.

exits.label: Take the lower path toward the dry sinkhole

nodes.title: The Frightened Mule Handler
nodes.page: Beside a dry stone drinking trough where the green algae has turned entirely to grey dust, a panicked mule handler frantically packs his empty crates onto a stubborn beast. He mutters curses under his breath while glancing back toward the barren horizon, eager to turn his animals away from the forbidding basin before the scorching noon heat sets in. Your grip tightens on the Seedkey hidden inside your tunic, its cold ceramic surface a sharp contrast to the stifling air. The handler pauses, casting a wary look at your pack and the glowing lantern at your belt.

nodes.brief: Along the white rim-track where the wind hums through fence wire, a traveling salt-boiler shares his dry bread and warns you about the quick-crust bogs hidden near the shore.

exits.label: Venture between the towering gypsum dunes
Approach the rusted drop-bars of the gate
Follow the bubbling mineral vent ahead

nodes.title: The Salt-Boiler's Warning
nodes.page: Along the white rim-track where the desert wind hums monotonously through rusted fence wire, a traveling salt-boiler sits cross-legged, sharing a heel of dry, rock-hard bread. He points a stained finger toward the shimmering expanse below, warning you about treacherous quick-crust bogs that swallow unwary travelers whole near the shore. Your ember-lamp flickers slightly in a sudden gust, casting dancing shadows across the cracked earth. The boiler finishes his crust, wiping his hands on his trousers as he watches you weigh his words.

nodes.brief: Beneath a jagged cliff of fused grey glass, an old scavenger named Hobb sorts through a heap of rusted iron hoops and offers you a crooked iron needle for your pack.

exits.label: Continue between the tall gypsum dunes

nodes.title: The Scavenger's Offering
nodes.page: Beneath a jagged cliff of fused grey glass that glints fiercely in the sunlight, an old scavenger named Hobb sorts through a massive heap of twisted iron hoops. He holds up a crooked iron needle, squinting through rheumy eyes as he offers it to you for your travel pack. The air smells sharply of sulfur and baked earth, and your lamp emits a soft, rhythmic ticking as the coals settle inside their iron housing. Hobb waits patiently, tapping the rusty needle against his knee while he sizes up your journey.

nodes.brief: Near a row of abandoned stone watch-cabins, a nervous teamster warns you that the Salt Court patrols have been seizing stray lanterns and taxing every drop of fuel.

exits.label: Head toward the abandoned toll-gate
Seek shelter near the bronze weather-vane

nodes.title: The Watch-Cabin Warning
nodes.page: Near a row of abandoned stone watch-cabins with shattered windows, a nervous teamster crouches in the meager shade, whispering tales of greedy Salt Court patrols. He warns you that their riders have been seizing stray lanterns and imposing cruel taxes on every drop of fuel carried across the rim. Your hand instinctively brushes against the warm iron of your own ember-lamp, guarding the vital fire within. The teamster glances nervously up the trail, urging you to keep your head down and your pace steady.

nodes.brief: By the rusted hulk of an ore-crusher stranded in the white dust, a solitary woman tends a small fire of dried camel dung and watches the northern horizon for dust-devils.

exits.label: Pass through the old toll-gate aprons
Follow the path toward the mineral spring

nodes.title: The Ore-Crusher Camp
nodes.page: By the rusted hulk of an ancient ore-crusher stranded amid endless white dust, a solitary woman tends a small, smokeless fire of dried camel dung. She stares intently at the northern horizon, tracking the slow crawl of distant dust-devils with practiced calm. Your boots crunch softly on the salt-crust as you approach, drawing a sidelong glance from her weathered, sun-darkened face. She gestures vaguely toward the tracks stretching out beyond the iron ruin.

nodes.brief: On a limestone shelf overlooking the shimmering flats, a young apprentice from the mirror-guild practices flashing signals with a pocket looking-glass while her master sleeps.

exits.label: Walk toward the rusted iron drop-bars
Head past the bubbling mineral water vent

nodes.title: The Young Apprentice
nodes.page: On a limestone shelf overlooking the shimmering, bleached flats, a young mirror-guild apprentice practices flashing signals with a pocket looking-glass while her master sleeps nearby. Quick flashes of reflected sunlight dance across the rocky ground, spelling out silent messages to the distant towers. Your ember-lamp radiates a steady, quiet heat against your hip, unnoticed amid the blinding glare. The apprentice lowers her glass for a moment, watching you curiously with bright, alert eyes.

nodes.brief: Beside a cairn of white stones marking a traveler's grave, a stray dog sniffs the dry earth and follows your boots with hungry, unblinking yellow eyes.

exits.label: Make your way toward the weather-vane
Inspect the deep rock-cut cistern

nodes.title: The Stray's Vigil
nodes.page: Beside a lonely cairn of white stones marking an anonymous traveler's grave, a thin stray dog sniffs the dry earth before fixing its hungry, unblinking yellow eyes upon your boots. The silence of the basin presses down heavily, broken only by the faint crackle of coals inside your lantern. The animal takes a tentative step forward, whining softly as it measures the distance between you and its next meal. You adjust the straps of your pack and prepare your next move.

nodes.brief: Under the broken lintel of an old customs post, a disgruntled tax-watcher counts his remaining copper slugs and wonders aloud if the rainy season will wash away his ledgers.

exits.label: Walk past the crooked iron drop-bars
Follow the sign toward the mineral vent
Rest near the silent bronze weather-vane

nodes.title: The Disgruntled Tax-Watcher
nodes.page: Under the broken lintel of an old customs post, a disgruntled tax-watcher counts his remaining copper slugs and wonders aloud if the coming rainy season will wash away his useless ledgers. The wooden desk before him is warped and cracked by years of merciless sun. Your lamp casts a warm, flickering glow across the peeling paper notices tacked to the stone wall. He looks up from his coins, offering a cynical grimace at your laden pack.

nodes.brief: At the foot of the zig-zag goat path leading down to the salt-crust, an exhausted trader rests his bleeding heels and advises you to wrap your ankles in double linen.

exits.label: Step out onto the windswept terrace edge
Examine the open rock-cut cistern
Climb toward the escarpment mirror bank

nodes.title: The Exhausted Trader
nodes.page: At the foot of the steep, zig-zag goat path leading down onto the blinding salt-crust, an exhausted trader rests his bleeding heels and rubs his aching calves. He advises you earnestly to wrap your ankles in double layers of linen if you hope to survive the abrasive flats without crippling blisters. Your ember-lamp hangs at your belt, a warm anchor across the desolate landscape. The trader pulls a fresh strip of cloth from his pouch, nodding encouragingly as you survey the descent.

nodes.brief: Beside a sulfurous mud-pot that spits grey bubbles, a lonely hermit trades a pinch of dried salt-bush leaves for a swallow of the water-skin hanging at your belt.

exits.label: Trade a mouthful of water for the grey leaves.
Refuse the trade and step past the bubbling vent.

nodes.title: The Sulfur Vent
nodes.page:
Grey bubbles rupture with a wet pop in the sulfurous mud-pot, releasing a thick breath of rotten eggs into the dry air. A lonely hermit squats upon a flat slab of shale nearby, fingers trembling as he offers a pinch of crumpled, sun-baked salt-bush leaves in exchange for a single moisture-filled swallow from the water-skin at your belt. His eyes are milky with age, yet they follow the shape of your canvas pack with sharp intent.

You consider whether to trade your water for his bitter greens or keep moving along the gravel trail before the sun reaches its zenith.

nodes.brief: Within the hollow of a wind-scoured limestone arch, a family of displaced herders cluster around a cold hearth and watch you pass with silent, guarded suspicion.

exits.label: Walk past the silent herders without breaking stride.

nodes.title: The Limestone Arch
nodes.page: Wind howls through the hollow cavity of the limestone arch, scouring away the loose sand and leaving only bare, pale rock. A family of displaced herders huddles close together around a cold, unlit hearth of blackened stones, watching your approach with heavy, guarded silence. Their sheep-dogs lie motionless at their feet, too weak from the drought to raise their heads as you draw near.

nodes.brief: On a high gravel ridge where the wind strips the salt from the bushes, an old cart-axle lies broken across the track like the limb of some fallen iron beast.

exits.label: Step carefully around the rusted iron and press onward.
Search the wreckage for any dropped tools or usable metal.

nodes.title: The Broken Axle
nodes.page: Snapped across the gravel track, an iron cart-axle lies like the limb of some fallen beast, spokes half-buried in drifting white dust. On this high ridge, the wind tears fiercely at your cloak, stripping the salt crust from the sparse desert bushes and pelting your boots with tiny pebbles. The shattered remains of the wagon offer no shelter, only a grim reminder of how cargo turns to ruin under this unsparing sky.

nodes.brief: Beneath a cliff overhang streaked with orange mineral stains, a wicker basket full of dried dates hangs from a iron hook, left by charitable pilgrims for passing runners.

exits.label: Take a few dates from the hanging basket.
Leave the pilgrims' offering untouched and keep walking.

nodes.title: The Cliffside Basket
nodes.page: Orange mineral stains streak the grey cliff face above like dried rust, dripping down toward a weathered wicker basket suspended from a thick iron hook. Pilgrims have left this token for passing runners, and inside lie a handful of wrinkled, sugar-crusted dates wrapped in greasy parchment. The shade beneath the overhang offers a brief respite from the relentless glare bouncing off the salt below.

nodes.brief: By the edge of a dry sinkhole where the white crust ripples like frozen water, a discarded mule skeleton grins up at the cloudless, blazing vault of the sky.

exits.label: Circle wide around the rim to avoid the crumbling edge.

nodes.title: The Dry Sinkhole
nodes.page: The white crust around the dry sinkhole ripples in concentric circles like frozen water, marking where the earth once swallowed a careless traveler whole. At the bottom of the depression, a bleached mule skeleton grins up toward the cloudless, blazing vault of the sky with empty eye sockets. The air here smells faintly of ancient dust and baked lime, devoid of any living sound.

nodes.brief: Where the rim-road narrows between two towering dunes of white gypsum, the tracks of heavy iron-shod salt-wagons converge into a single deeply gouged trough.

exits.label: Follow the wagon ruts deeper into the narrows.

nodes.title: The Gypsum Canyons
nodes.page: Two towering dunes of pure white gypsum pinch the rim-road into a narrow corridor, reflecting the blinding morning glare with searing intensity. Deeply gouged tracks from heavy iron-shod salt-wagons converge here into a single rutted trough that cuts straight through the pale sand. The passage feels like walking through the throat of an hourglass where time itself has turned to salt.

nodes.brief: On the gravel apron before the abandoned toll-gate, three rusted iron drop-bars hang crooked from their chains across the dusty path to the open basin.

exits.label: Step beneath the crooked iron bars into the open basin.
Pause to search the littered guardhouse floor for dropped coin.
Turn back to check the side-tracks leading along the ridge.

nodes.title: The Abandoned Toll-Gate
nodes.page: Three rusted iron drop-bars hang crooked from their snapped chains, swinging gently in the hot breeze before the abandoned toll-gate. The gravel apron is littered with discarded copper tallies and broken ledger boards buried half an inch deep in fine dust. Beyond this broken threshold, the open basin spreads out in a blinding sheet of white all the way to the distant horizon.

nodes.brief: Beside a bubbling vent of warm mineral water that tastes of alum, a faded wooden sign points the way toward the central observatory across four days of salt.

exits.label: Follow the wooden sign's pointing finger onto the salt flats.
Stoop to cool your burning hands in the mineral stream.

nodes.title: The Alum Spring
nodes.page: Warm mineral water bubbles up from a jagged fissure in the rock, smelling faintly of alum and leaving a yellow crust along its miniature banks. A weathered wooden sign, bleached grey by decades of sun, points its splintered finger across four days of salt toward the central observatory. The heat rising from the spring wraps around your ankles like a physical weight.

nodes.brief: Under the shadow of a colossal bronze weather-vane that no longer turns, a cluster of travelers' bedrolls marks the last sheltered campsite before the true desert begins.

exits.label: Inspect the abandoned bedrolls for anything useful left behind.
Walk past the silent monument and step out onto the crust.

nodes.title: The Bronze Vane
nodes.page: A colossal bronze weather-vane shaped like a winged lizard towers overhead, its frozen tail pointing permanently toward the west while the pivot below is rusted solid. Beneath its massive shadow, a tangled cluster of discarded travelers' bedrolls marks the last sheltered campsite before the true desert begins. A few cold embers lie scattered in the dirt among empty oil flasks and shredded sandals.

nodes.brief: Where the limestone terrace breaks into a sheer drop over the grey salt-flats, a stone bench carved by forgotten engineers offers a final sweeping view of the dead sea.

exits.label: Rest your aching legs briefly on the carved stone bench.
Pick your way down the steep goat trail toward the flats.

nodes.title: The Limestone Terrace
nodes.page: The limestone terrace breaks away abruptly into a sheer drop over the grey salt-flats, offering a final, sweeping panorama of the dead sea below. A stone bench carved by forgotten engineers sits near the edge, its surface worn smooth by the rumps of countless weary pilgrims who sat here to gaze at the shimmering mirages. From up here, Prism looks like a cluster of jagged glass teeth stuck in a bowl of milk.

nodes.brief: Beside a deep rock-cut cistern whose iron grille has been wrenched off by thieves, a discarded traveler's ledger lies open to pages bleached entirely blank by the sun.

exits.label: Step past the open cistern and descend toward the lower track.
Follow the narrow goat path winding down to the dust.
Turn back toward the limestone watchtower.

nodes.title: The Bleached Pages
nodes.page: Beside a deep rock-cut cistern whose iron grille has been wrenched off by thieves, a discarded traveler's ledger lies open to pages bleached entirely blank by the sun. The dry wind rattles the stiff parchment edges like dry leaves, while below in the dark stone well, water laps against green slime with a hollow, teasing sound. Your fingers tighten around the cold ceramic key in your pack as you consider whether to linger by the water-hole or retrace your steps toward the perimeter wall.

nodes.brief: On the windswept shoulder of the western escarpment, a bank of solar mirrors catches the morning glare and throws blinding shards of white light across the lower track.

exits.label: Pick your way carefully down the sun-drenched slope.

nodes.title: The Solar Glare
nodes.page: On the windswept shoulder of the western escarpment, a bank of solar mirrors catches the morning glare and throws blinding shards of white light across the lower track. The angled brass frames hum faintly under the heat, focusing stray rays into burning focal points that dance over the grey dust. Squinting against the brilliant reflection, you grip your ember-lamp tighter as you look for a secure footing down the steep, chalky slope.

nodes.brief: Where the wagon road finally descends onto the flat crust of the Basin, a lonely stone milestone marked with eroded ancient numbers stands half-buried in drifting powder.

exits.label: March straight onto the blinding white expanse.
Follow the wheel ruts curving toward the lower basin.

nodes.title: The Milestone
nodes.page: Where the wagon road finally descends onto the flat crust of the Basin, a lonely stone milestone marked with eroded ancient numbers stands half-buried in drifting powder. Salt crystals crust its weathered face, blurring the destination carvings that once pointed travelers toward the glass cities of the interior. The air grows noticeably drier here, carrying the faint, metallic taste of old brine and sun-baked dust.

nodes.brief: At the Lamp-Post Gate where the iron lanterns are being snuffed for the day, the wry glass-diver Calder leans against a stone pillar and cleans his salt-goggles with an oily rag.

exits.label: Press on into the widening glare.

nodes.title: The Lamp-Post Gate
nodes.page: At the Lamp-Post Gate where the iron lanterns are being snuffed for the day, the wry glass-diver Calder leans against a stone pillar and cleans his salt-goggles with an oily rag. He watches you approach with one eyebrow arched in quiet amusement, his canvas pack resting squarely against his boots. The morning air smells of tallow smoke and dry earth, marking the absolute edge of the town's failing harvest.

nodes.brief: By the heavy timber gates of Candlemere, Calder sits on an overturned oil keg whistling a dry tune while tossing a heavy brass sounding-lead from hand to hand.

exits.label: Press on past the timber barricade.

nodes.title: The Oil Keg
nodes.page: At Candlemere's timber gates, Calder sits on an overturned oil keg whistling a dry tune while tossing a brass sounding-lead from hand to hand. The rhythmic clink of metal against brass echoes softly against the grain of the reinforced wood. He pauses as your shadow falls across his boots, offering a crooked, knowing grin that betrays his familiarity with the treacherous flats ahead.

nodes.brief: Under the iron arch of the western gatehouse, Calder adjusts his wide-brimmed wicker hat and asks if you are fool enough to cross the white flats without a guide.

exits.label: Press on toward the open Basin.

nodes.title: The Western Gatehouse
nodes.page: Under the iron arch of the western gatehouse, Calder adjusts his wide-brimmed wicker hat and asks if you are fool enough to cross the white flats without a guide. His salt-crusted canvas jacket smells faintly of old brine and dried kelp, marking him as someone who knows the perilous shifting crust of the old sea. He taps the side of his copper map-tube with a calloused thumb, waiting for your answer.

nodes.brief: In the dust just outside the guarded portal, Calder stands with his canvas pack already strapped tight, offering a crooked grin and a weathered copper map-tube if you need him.

exits.label: Press on into the bright haze.

nodes.title: The Guarded Portal
nodes.page: In the dust just beyond the heavy gates, Calder stands with his canvas pack already strapped tight, offering a crooked grin and a weathered copper map-tube if you need him. The distant salt-flats shimmer behind him like a vast sheet of hammered tin under the mounting sun. He shifts his weight onto one heel, balancing an ash-wood pole across his shoulder with casual expertise.

nodes.brief: Beside the tallow-scratched gatepost, Calder offers a weather-cracked hand to guide you across the white flats for half a copper jar.

exits.label: Follow Calder as he strides onto the white salt.
Stay close behind your guide as a salt-clogged cart looms ahead.
Step out independently with the glass-diver at your shoulder.

nodes.title: The Weather-Cracked Hand
nodes.page: Beside the tallow-scratched gatepost, Calder offers a weather-cracked hand to guide you across the white flats for half a copper jar. His dry laugh cuts through the morning silence as he slings his canvas pack higher onto his shoulder and adjusts his wide-brimmed hat. Together, you step off the solid stone of the rim road and onto the dazzling, brittle crust of the dead sea.

nodes.brief: You turn your back on the glass-diver's grin, stepping past the iron post alone into the grey haze of the Rim Road.

exits.label: Dodge the kelp-laden mule and press deeper into the grey haze
Wait by the cistern-house to heed the glass-diver's last warning
Stride past the cattle-pound unescorted with the key held tight

nodes.title: The Grey Rim Road
nodes.page:
Solitary footsteps crunch across the alkaline dust as the iron gate of Candlemere shrinks into the shimmering distance. Your ember-lamp swings from your wrist, its banked coals casting a faint, rhythmic glow against the grey expanse of the Rim Road. Behind you, the glass-diver's laughter fades beneath the dry whistling of the wind through abandoned water-scaffolds. The vast, salt-crusted bed of the dead sea stretches eastward like an unwritten page, promising little save for mirage and distance.

Ahead, the track divides where a milestone of fused green glass leans drunkenly into the alkali.

nodes.brief: Under the eaves of the tallow-sellers, Calder tests the weight of your copper while grease-smoke curls from a copper brazier.

exits.label: Inspect the mule-track with Calder
Exchange sharp words with the tinker
Step past the kiln ahead of your guide

nodes.title: The Tallow-Sellers' Eaves
nodes.page:
Under the low thatch of the tallow-sellers, grease-smoke curls thick and sweet from a copper brazier while Calder tests the weight of your silver coin against his knuckles. The glass-diver flips the metal once, listening for the sharp ring of true silver-alloy before sliding it deep into his waistcoat pocket with a knowing nod. Around you, the market noise of Candlemere fades against the relentless dry wind whispering off the white rim.

You tighten the straps of your wool coat over the cold ceramic key hidden in your lining, your eyes fixed on the hazy expanse of the Basin stretching out beyond the rim road. Calder slings his narrow iron-shod staff across his shoulder, waiting to see which direction you intend to take as the dust settles around your boots.

nodes.brief: A salt-clogged cart blocks the cart-track, and Calder leans on an ash-pole to help you shove the timber aside.

exits.label: Huddle beneath the iron culvert
Share a roasted chicory root
Pass the green glass milestone

nodes.title: The Blocked Cart-Track
nodes.page:
A salt-clogged cart jams the narrow track, wooden axle splintered under a mound of crude alkaline blocks that glint cruelly in the sun. Calder leans his full weight against a sturdy ash-pole, planting his boots in the grit as he urges you to help shove the dead weight aside so the road ahead clears. The heat beats down from a cloudless sky, smelling strongly of old brine and sun-baked timber.

With a final heave, the wheel-hub clears the rut and spins free, kicking up a shower of glittering dust that settles on your gaiters. Calder wipes his brow with a greasy rag, nodding toward the diverging tracks that fork out toward the open white desert.

nodes.brief: Walking out alone, your boots crunch on dropped sheep-bells while the gate-warden spits a dry farewell into the dust.

exits.label: Pass the green glass milestone marking three leagues
Buy brackish water from a widow by the horse-trough
Scrape dried salt-cake while signal mirrors flash

nodes.title: Walking Out Alone
nodes.page:
Walking out alone past the iron gate of Candlemere, your boots crunch rhythmically over scattered sheep-bells left behind by the morning herds. The gate-warden stands by his post, spitting a dry, indifferent farewell into the alkaline dust before turning his back on your solitary departure. The vast white shell of the dried inland sea opens before you like an immense mirror reflecting the blinding afternoon glare.

You adjust the weight of your ember-lamp against your hip, feeling the banked coals shift safely inside their perforated iron housing. The horizon wavers behind shimmering heat-mirages where the shattered glass cities of the Old Lensfolk catch the light.

nodes.brief: You dodge a nervous mule laden with dried kelp, leaving Calder behind as the town walls shrink into the glare.

exits.label: Listen to a distant drover tune echo off limestone
Watch a tethered donkey rattle its iron ring
Marvel at the preserved whiskers of a dried hare

nodes.title: Dodging the Kelp Mule
nodes.page:
You dodge hard to the left as a nervous pack-mule laden with dried kelp lurches past, leaving Calder behind in the press of townfolk as the limestone walls of Candlemere shrink into the desert glare. The animal's iron bells jangle with a frantic, hollow rhythm that echoes off the low hills. You find yourself alone on the gravel path, the wind carrying the sharp scent of iodine and dry scrub.

Pressing onward into the open stretch of the Rim Road, solitude closes in on every side. Every footstep carries you further from the familiar tallow-smoke and stone hearths of home, drawing you deeper into the domain of the Salt Court.

nodes.brief: Calder catches your elbow by the cistern-house, pointing out a salt-squall curdling the eastern horizon before you commit.

exits.label: Inspect the wheel-rut gypsum crystals with Calder
Listen to the muffled thrum of a distant salt-mill
Trade rye bread with a ragged shepherd

nodes.title: The Cistern-House Warning
nodes.page:
Calder catches your elbow with a calloused hand by the moss-grown cistern-house, pulling you back into the shadow of the stone water-trough. He points a sun-darkened finger toward the eastern horizon, where a thick, yellowish salt-squall is rapidly curdling the sky into an angry haze. The wind dies down completely for a breathless heartbeat, replaced by an eerie, heavy stillness that makes the hairs on your arms stand on end.

The coming blow promises to scour the flats clean of any traveller foolish enough to cross without cover. Calder looks sideways at you, waiting to see how you intend to weather the approaching gale before committing your steps to the open track.

nodes.brief: You stride past the cattle-pound unescorted, your fingers curling around the cold ceramic key hidden in your wool coat.

exits.label: Trade rye bread with a ragged shepherd
Note the hermit chimney peeking above salt-drifts
Walk boot-to-boot through the narrow silt banks

nodes.title: The Cattle-Pound Passage
nodes.page:
You stride past the abandoned cattle-pound unescorted, your fingers curling protectively around the cold ceramic key hidden safely inside your wool coat lining. The dry wooden fences stand like bleached ribs against the alkaline earth, devoid of beasts or herdsmen in this punishing drought. Every breath tastes faintly of salt and baked lime, reminding you of the desperate harvest failure back at Candlemere.

Ahead, the road splits into faint wagon ruts that vanish into the shimmering distance of the Basin floor. You keep your pace steady and purposeful, knowing that the Seedkey must reach the Rain Vault before the monsoon floods the lowlands.

nodes.brief: Calder kicks a loose shard of window-slag aside on the mule-track, muttering about toll-collectors waiting near the dry ford.

exits.label: Hear a grim tale beside the lime-kiln
Adjust your pack in the wheel-wright's shack

nodes.title: The Mule-Track Shards
nodes.page:
Calder kicks a loose, jagged shard of window-slag aside on the dusty mule-track, sending it skittering across the white crust with a thin, metallic ring. He mutters a low curse under his breath, warning that toll-collectors from the Salt Court have been spotted watching the dry ford ahead for unwary travellers. The air here smells of sulphur and sun-baked glass, thick with the heat radiating off the ancient lake-bed.

You check the iron housing of your ember-lamp to ensure the banked coals are secure before pressing forward into the shadow of the crumbling ruins. Every shadow along the track looks like a mounted guard waiting to demand exorbitant passage fees.

nodes.brief: You trade insults with a crusty tinker mending a copper kettle by the ditch while Calder inspects his compass-dial.

exits.label: Hear a grim tale beside the lime-kiln
Adjust your pack in the wheel-wright's shack

nodes.title: The Tinkering Dispute
nodes.page:
You trade sharp insults with a crusty tinker who is busy hammering a dented copper kettle beside the drainage ditch, while Calder methodically inspects his brass compass-dial. The tinker spits into the dirt, complaining bitterly about the rising price of charcoal and the cruelty of the local toll-lords. Calder ignores the grumbling, tapping the glass face of his instrument until the needle settles true toward the southeast.

Leaving the disgruntled artisan to his hammering, you follow your guide away from the ditch as the track begins to slope downward toward the sun-bleached expanse of the Basin floor. The distant towers of Prism glimmer like broken teeth on the horizon.

nodes.brief: A three-legged cur trails your boots past the abandoned kiln, its tongue lolling dryly in the baking noon heat.

exits.label: Duck behind fence-hurdles as riders pass
Jump as a startled kestrel launches from a post

nodes.title: The Three-Legged Cur
nodes.page:
A mangy, three-legged cur trails closely behind your boots past the abandoned lime-kiln, its tongue lolling dryly in the baking noon heat as it pants for moisture. The poor beast begs with milky, rheumy eyes, but your own skin-flask holds barely enough brackish water to sustain your own march across the flats. The crumbling stone oven radiates a dry, stifling warmth that makes the surrounding air ripple like water.

You step up your pace to shake off the persistent animal, keeping your eyes on the winding track ahead where the horizon blurs into a brilliant, salt-caked glare. Prism's spires rise faintly in the far distance.

nodes.brief: You huddle beneath an iron-beamed culvert as a salt-cart rumbles past, kicking up a choking cloud of alkaline dust.

exits.label: Pocket a copper eyelet dropped by a runner

nodes.title: The Iron Culvert
nodes.page:
Under the culvert's rust-flaking iron beams you huddle as a salt-cart rumbles overhead and alkaline dust coats the back of your throat in a dense choking cloud. The wooden wheels groan under their immense burden, shaking the very earth beneath your boots until the cart passes into silence. The taste of salt and iron hangs heavy on your tongue.

Crawling out from the shadowy shelter into the blinding glare, you brush the fine white powder from your sleeves and adjust your pack. The road ahead stretches straight and white toward the shimmering heart of the Saltglass Basin.

nodes.brief: Calder shares a roasted chicory root from his leather wallet while you check the hemp straps of your water-cask.

exits.label: Duck through the fence-hurdles to slip past mounted riders
Pocket the copper shoe-eyelet Calder found and press onward
Follow the lonely ridge where the kestrel flew

nodes.title: The Glass-Diver's Share
nodes.page:
Calder splits a roasted chicory root from his battered leather wallet, offering you the bitterer half while your thumbs test the hemp straps of your water-cask. The dry heat pulls moisture from every pore, but the roots keep the tongue active against the alkaline dust.

The road stretches ahead through the blinding white glare of the salt flats, empty save for the heat-shimmers dancing over the abandoned boundary stones.

nodes.brief: Solitary and brisk, you pass a milestone carved from green bottle-glass that marks three leagues from Candlemere's church.

exits.label: Retrieve the lost copper eyelet from the dust and continue
Share lukewarm tin-flask water while scanning the pale mirage flats
Turn back toward the lamp-town shadows

nodes.title: The Bottle-Glass Milestone
nodes.page:
Solitary and brisk, you pass a stout milestone carved from green bottle-glass that marks exactly three leagues from Candlemere's tilting church tower. The transparent pillar glows with trapped bubbles from a forgotten kiln, casting pale emerald light across the grey gravel of the Rim Road.

The horizon wavers beneath a shimmering wall of dry air, blurring the distance where the vast salt basin begins. You pause by the glassy post to weigh your next stride.

nodes.brief: A widow sells parched beans from a tin bucket by the horse-trough, asking double for a cup of brackish well-water.

exits.label: Inspect the warning sign nailed to the nearby rail
Step past the ditch-diggers clearing choked stone culverts

nodes.title: The Parched Well-Head
nodes.page:
A weary widow sits by the horse-trough selling parched beans from a greasy tin bucket, demanding double coin for a single cup of brackish well-water. Her skin is baked the colour of dried clay, and her fingers tremble as she measures out the meagre portions to passing runners.

The smell of stagnant lime water hangs heavy in the still noon air.

nodes.brief: You pause to scrape dried salt-cake from your gaiters while distant signal mirrors flash three sharp warnings from a ridge.

exits.label: Read the decree nailed near the dry well-head
Watch Calder test the hollow crust beside the track

nodes.title: Signals on the Ridge
nodes.page:
You pause on the alkaline slope to scrape thick, dried salt-cake from your gaiters with a flat slate shard. Far across the pale basin rim, distant signal mirrors flash three sharp warnings from a craggy limestone ridge, cutting bright arcs through the hazy blue sky.

The coded flashes hint at watchers guarding the approaches to Prism. You gather your pack straps tighter against your shoulders as you weigh the path ahead.

nodes.brief: Calder whistles an old drover's tune that skips off the limestone banks, keeping your lagging spirits steady against the sun.

exits.label: Pass the weary ditch-diggers clearing alkali silt

nodes.title: Drover's Tune
nodes.page:
Calder whistles an old, skipping drover's tune that bounces off the bleached limestone banks, lifting your lagging spirits against the merciless glare of the sun. The ancient melody speaks of green pastures that haven't existed since the great drying began.

The dust devils swirl around your boots as the road winds deeper into the sun-baked hills. You keep step with the music, looking ahead to where the path narrows.

nodes.brief: A tethered donkey brays at your passing shadow, rattling its iron ring against a stunted thorn-tree in the gully.

exits.label: Walk past the ditch-diggers labouring with wooden shovels
Count your heavy paces against the rhythmic crunch of gravel
Watch Calder point toward the distant charcoal burners' smoke
Turn back toward the safety of the western rim

nodes.title: The Tethered Beast
nodes.page:
A tethered donkey brays sharply at your passing shadow, rattling its iron neck-ring against the trunk of a stunted, grey thorn-tree in the dry gully. The animal's ribs show like barrel hoops beneath a coat stiffened by wind-blown salt.

The gully offers a moment of brief, dusty shade before the road climbs back into the open glare. You study the diverging tracks branching out beyond the thorn-tree.

nodes.brief: You step over the carcass of a dried hare, marveling at how the salt has preserved its whiskers like copper wire.

exits.label: Keep counting your rhythmic paces against the gravel
Follow Calder's gaze toward the smudge of distant smoke

nodes.title: The Wire-Whiskered Hare
nodes.page:
You step carefully over the stiffened carcass of a desert hare, marvelling at how the concentrated salt has preserved its long whiskers like fine copper wire. Its unblinking eyes have glazed into tiny beads of clouded amber under the relentless sun.

The empty track stretches onward through the silent basin borderlands.

nodes.brief: Calder kneels to inspect a wheel-rut filled with glittering gypsum crystals, warning you that heavy wagons have cut deep traps.

exits.label: Steer clear of the buried glass lintel ahead
Buy dried locusts from the ragged boy selling them on a stalk

nodes.title: Gypsum Traps
nodes.page:
Calder drops to one knee to inspect a deep wheel-rut filled with glittering gypsum crystals, warning you that heavy freight wagons have cut treacherous traps into the crust. The razor-edged mineral can slice through stout boot leather with a single misstep.

The bright morning glare makes the crystalline rime sparkle with deceptive beauty. You watch your footing carefully as you weigh the safest course around the fracture.

nodes.brief: Walking alone, you hear the muffled thrum of a distant salt-mill grinding through the windless afternoon silence.

exits.label: Head toward the smudge of smoke from the earthen pits
Avoid the buried green glass remnant of the old farmstead
Buy dried locusts from the ragged boy by the track
Take the reckless way

nodes.title: The Distant Mill
nodes.page:
Walking entirely alone, you catch the muffled grind of a distant salt-mill working its stones through the windless afternoon silence. The mechanical groan vibrates up through the soles of your boots like the heartbeat of a sleeping leviathan.

The open track offers several distinct directions as the grinding noise fades into the dry air. You consider your options before taking another step into the heat.

nodes.brief: You trade a crust of rye bread with a ragged shepherd whose sheep have wool stiffened with alkaline crust.

exits.label: Let Calder wipe the alkaline rime from your stinging eyelids
Pause by the dry stone wall where wild caper bushes cling

nodes.title: The Shepherding Trade
nodes.page:
You trade a crust of dry rye bread from your pocket with a ragged shepherd whose sheep have wool stiffened into solid plates of alkaline crust. He points wordlessly toward the shimmering horizon with a crook made of polished juniper wood.

The trade leaves your pack a little lighter, but the local knowledge is worth the sacrifice of grain. You survey the branching tracks before you move on.

nodes.brief: Calder points out a chimney peeking above the salt-drifts where a hermit once boiled seawater for tax-free crystals.

exits.label: Let Calder clear the rime from your eyes
Step toward the dry stone wall and wild capers

nodes.title: The Salt-Boiler's Chimney
nodes.page:
Salt-encrusted hummocks rise around a crooked brick chimney that barely clears the blinding white drifts of the basin floor. Calder points his knuckle toward the soot-stained opening where a fugitive hermit once boiled brine for tax-free crystals. The baked earth here smells faintly of sulphur and stale wood-ash, a lonely marker left behind by men who tried to cheat the toll-lords.

Your boots crunch against the brittle ground while you weigh whether to press deeper into the glare or seek a moment's shelter near the ruin.

nodes.brief: The track narrows between two high banks of wind-piled silt, forcing you to walk boot-to-boot with your hired guide.

exits.label: Listen to the singing glass vibrate in the stillness

nodes.title: The Narrow Silt-Banks
nodes.page:
Towering ramparts of wind-piled silt close in on either side, pinching the cart-track until it becomes a narrow trench of grey dust and shadow. You walk boot-to-boot with Calder, the two of you kicking up fine clouds of alkaline powder that cling to your woollen trousers. Between the high banks the silence sits close and enclosed, smelling of ancient dust and sun-baked clay.

A sudden hush falls over the trench as the wind dies completely, leaving only the sound of your own measured breathing.

nodes.brief: Beside a crumbling lime-kiln, Calder tells a grim tale of the Salt Court's enforcers collecting teeth for back-taxes.

exits.label: Douse the lantern before the ridge-sentries spot you
Crouch behind the stacked slate windbreak to think
Reach for your tinder-box in the gathering gloom

nodes.title: The Lime-Kiln Tale
nodes.page:
Crumbling white stone forms the hollow shell of an old lime-kiln, its interior stained by centuries of intense heat. Beside the ruined hearth, Calder spins a low-voiced yarn about the Salt Court enforcers who once patrolled these flats demanding molar teeth as collateral for unpaid extraction taxes. The dry air seems to tighten around his words, carrying the ghost-scent of wood smoke and old terror.

Shadows lengthen across the lime-floor, reminding you that the open basin grows unforgiving once the sun dips.

nodes.brief: A wheel-wright's abandoned shack offers a scrap of shade where you adjust your pack-straps before the basin opens.

exits.label: Extinguish the lantern coals before the glass-sentries watch

nodes.title: The Wheel-Wright's Shack
nodes.page:
Weather-beated timber planks lean together at drunken angles to form the skeletal shell of an abandoned wheel-wright's shed. Inside the meagre patch of shade, you shrug off your heavy travelling sack to adjust the chafing leather straps across your sore shoulders. Fine salt dust coats the floorboards like drifted snow, undisturbed save for the tracks of desert beetles.

The open basin glares just beyond the doorway, daring you to take the next punishing step into the light.

nodes.brief: You duck behind a stacked pile of fence-hurdles as three Salt Court riders trot past on long-legged desert ponies.

exits.label: Slip away toward the slate ridge
Wait until full dusk before moving

nodes.title: The Salt Court Riders
nodes.page: Three riders from the Salt Court trot past on long-legged desert ponies, their brass-trimmed saddles jingling rhythmically against the dry alkali wind. You duck flat behind a stacked pile of weathered fence-hurdles, holding your breath as the heavy scent of boiled mint and oiled leather drifts across the white dust. The lead rider pauses to adjust a silver-plated spyglass, scanning the jagged glass horizon where the Rim Road dips toward the dried seabed. Once the hoofbeats fade into the flat distance, you rise slowly from the grit, dusting off your wool tunic and weighing your next step along the whitening trail.

nodes.brief: Calder stoops to pick up a copper shoe-eyelet dropped by an earlier runner, pocketing it with a cynical wink.

exits.label: Crouch behind the stacked slate to check your gear
Prepare your tinder-box as the cold evening draft rises

nodes.title: The Copper Eyelet
nodes.page:
Sunlight glints off a tiny scrap of metal half-buried in the alkaline dust near the path. Calder stoops with a practiced creak of his leather jerkin, plucking a small copper shoe-eyelet dropped by some forgotten runner before you. He pockets the trinket with a cynical wink, muttering that every bit of salvage tells a story of someone who walked too fast or packed too light.

The vast white flats stretch onward under an unyielding sky, silent and indifferent to small gains.

nodes.brief: Walking without company, you jump as a startled kestrel launches from a hollow fence-post into the glaring blue sky.

exits.label: Strike your tinder-box against the deepening evening chill
Watch the sand-grouse scatter into the dry gully

nodes.title: The Startled Kestrel
nodes.page:
Walking entirely alone through the blistering silence, you jump as a brown kestrel erupts from a hollow fence-post with a sharp cry. Its wings beat furiously against the dry air before it catches a thermal and spirals up into the glaring blue dome of the sky. Your heart hammers against your ribs from the sudden shock, leaving you acutely aware of your own isolation on the rim.

The first pale violet shadows begin to stretch long and thin across the white salt.

nodes.brief: You share a mouthful of lukewarm water from your tin flask while Calder scans the white flats for mirage-shimmers.

exits.label: Hide your lantern light from the glass-sentries above
Reach for your tinder-box as the cold draft stirs

nodes.title: The Tin Flask
nodes.page:
Warm metal touches your cracked lips as you unscrew the tin flask and share a meager mouthful of lukewarm water with your guide. Calder wipes his mouth with the back of a calloused hand while his pale eyes sweep the shimmering white flats for mirage-tricks. The taste of tin and flat well-water does little to quench the salt-thirst coating your tongue, but it steadies your legs for the miles ahead.

The horizon wavers and bends under layers of superheated air, blurring the line between salt-crust and sky.

nodes.brief: A faded sign nailed to a fence-rail warns travelers that all dry wells belong by decree to the Salt Court.

exits.label: Reach for your tinder-box as the evening draft rises
Listen to Calder tap the iron casing of your lantern
Turn back toward the gate-warden and leave the basin

nodes.title: The Court Decree
nodes.page:
A warped plank of cedar nailed to a weathered fence-rail bears the deep-burned brand of the Salt Court, warning all travelers that every dry well within the basin belongs by decree to the toll-lords. The faded words read like a threat carved into wood, reminding you that water here is a crime unless bought with silver or blood.

The track forks ahead, offering a chance to retrace your steps or plunge deeper into the forbidden flats.

nodes.brief: Calder uses his iron-shod staff to test the crust of a suspicious sinkhole yawning beside the cart-track.

exits.label: heed Calder's warning about well-thieves and mirror-sentries
Check your flint and steel at the trackless crossroads

nodes.title: The Iron Staff
nodes.page:
Dust devils spin lazy spirals across the abandoned cart-track while Calder uses his heavy iron-shod staff to test the crust of a suspicious sinkhole yawning nearby. The wood-and-iron pole punches through the hollow crust with a brittle snap, revealing a dark drop where ancient brine once pooled beneath the salt. He steps back with a dry whistle, shaking dust from the iron tip.

The path ahead requires wary footing and a sharp eye for hidden traps in the white expanse.

nodes.brief: You pass a team of weary ditch-diggers clearing alkali silt from a choked stone culvert with wooden shovels.

exits.label: Prepare your flint and tinder for the dark
Listen to Calder warn of thieves and sentries
Watch the sand-grouse scatter into the gully

nodes.title: The Choked Culvert
nodes.page:
Laborers toil with broad wooden shovels, heaving grey alkali silt from a choked stone culvert that once drained the rim hills. Their foreman wipes salt-crust from his forehead with a grease-rag, offering a gloomy nod as you pass. The cold ceramic Seedkey shifts heavily against your ribs beneath your woolen tunic.

With the afternoon fading fast, you must decide how to navigate the tightening gloom and the watchful eyes of the basin.

nodes.brief: Solitary and sweating, you count your paces against the rhythmic crunch of gravel beneath your heavy walking boots.

exits.label: Follow the startled birds toward the gully
Check your gear at the vanishing crossroads

nodes.title: Counting Paces
nodes.page:
Walking boots grind against dry gravel, a pace that helps drive away thoughts of the failing harvests back at Candlemere. Solitary under the glare, you count your paces while tracking the shimmering heat-hazes dancing across the flats. Sweat stings your eyes, but the ember-lamp stays firmly gripped in your leather-gloved hand.

Ahead, the trail divides into faint tracks that vanish into the bright salt waste.

nodes.brief: Calder points toward a distant smudge of smoke where charcoal burners are smothering scrub-oak in earthen pits.

exits.label: Press onward to the trackless basin crossroads

nodes.title: Smoke on the Rise
nodes.page:
Calder points a weathered finger toward a distant smudge of greasy grey smoke hovering above the scrub-line. Charcoal burners are smothering stunted oak in earthen pits to feed the distant glass-foundries. The acrid scent of burning roots drifts across the dry earth, mixing with the sharp tang of mineral dust.

You pause by the trackside to weigh your next move as the afternoon shadows lengthen.

nodes.brief: You stumble over a buried lintel of green glass, the remnant of some old farmstead swallowed by the creeping salt.

exits.label: Head toward the crossroads at the basin edge
Push forward as night falls over the white pan

nodes.title: Buried Glass
nodes.page:
A jagged edge of green glass pokes through the dusty soil, the lone remnant of some forgotten farmstead swallowed long ago by the creeping salt. You step carefully around the fused window-pane, mindful of your boots on the brittle shards. The wind carries a faint metallic tang from the interior ruins.

The path ahead frays into several faint directions as dusk approaches the white pan.

nodes.brief: A ragged boy runs alongside the track trying to sell dried locusts threaded on a grass stalk for a farthing.

exits.label: Walk toward the crossroads in the fading light
Watch the distant glass-sentries blink their signals

nodes.title: The Locust Seller
nodes.page:
A ragged boy darts alongside the cart-track, offering dried locusts threaded on a stiff grass stalk for a single farthing. He chatters eagerly about toll-lord patrols and sudden sinkholes before darting back into the thorny scrub. You adjust the heavy strap of your ember-lamp while digesting his hasty warning.

The dusty track ahead offers a couple of distinct paths into the gathering twilight.

nodes.brief: Calder dips a stained rag into his canteen to wipe the alkaline rime from your stinging, dust-reddened eyelids.

exits.label: Watch the Glasswrights exchange amber signals
Face the oncoming night at the edge of the pan

nodes.title: Salt in the Eyes
nodes.page:
Calder dips a damp rag into his canteen, pressing it gently against your stinging, dust-reddened eyelids to wash away the biting alkaline rime. The cool relief is fleeting as the desert breeze immediately coats your skin in fine mineral powder. The heavy iron-shod staff rests against his knee while he scans the horizon.

Across the darkening plain, distant lights begin to shift and answer one another.

nodes.brief: You pause by a dry stone wall where wild caper bushes cling desperately to the calcified mortar joints.

exits.label: Make for the crossroads where the cart-track ends
Look toward the amber flash of the night-watch
Step out onto the vast and silent white pan

nodes.title: Caper Bushes
nodes.page:
