nodes.title: The Chamber of Whispering Lenses
nodes.page:
Hundreds of curved, centuries-old mirrors catch your flickering lantern light, refracting a chaotic web of blinding beams across the damp stone floor. Every movement you make sends dazzling arcs of light dancing across the vaulted ceiling, accompanied by a faint, glassine hum like a swarm of metal bees. The brilliant glare makes it difficult to see where the walkways lead, forcing you to navigate by touch and instinct through the maze of optics.

The air smells of ozone and static electricity, and you must choose which reflected pathway to follow into the dark.

nodes.brief: Beside a collapsed scaffolding of copper pipes, you salvage a length of rigid tubing to wedge against the jammed secondary locking mechanism.

exits.label: Walk toward the green glass vault
Step into the condensing tower's shadow

nodes.title: The Scaffolding Wedge
nodes.page:
Rusted copper pipes groan and shift as you wrench a sturdy length of rigid tubing free from the collapsed scaffolding overhead. Wedging the metal bar firmly against the jammed secondary locking mechanism, you throw your weight against it until the stubborn gears finally give way with a metallic shriek. Dust billows from the housing, revealing a narrow service gap large enough to squeeze through.

The subterranean chill bites at your skin, and the distant rumble of the approaching rains warns you that time is running out.

nodes.brief: Within the alcove dedicated to the forgotten rain-seers, a dry basin waits for an offering that you must decide whether to give or withhold.

exits.label: Follow the dried salt crystal trail
Inspect the humming lift shaft dynamo
Examine the weeping statues' basin

nodes.title: The Dry Basin of Rain-Seers
nodes.page:
Carved images of long-forgotten rain-seers stare down from the walls of the alcove, their stone eyes fixed upon an empty stone basin in the center of the floor. A faint residue of old offerings cakes the bottom, waiting for you to decide whether to leave something of value or pass by with empty hands. The silence here is absolute, save for the steady drip of condensation somewhere in the deeper masonry.

Every instinct tells you that the basin demands a token of your journey before it will grant safe passage further into the vaults.

nodes.brief: Across the trembling glass bridge spanning the deep subterranean shaft, a rising gale from the impending monsoon whistles through the iron struts.

exits.label: Cross toward the obsidian floor
Head for the humming lift dynamo
Seek out the weeping statues

nodes.title: The Glass Bridge Gale
nodes.page:
A rising gale from the impending monsoon shrieks through the iron struts of the trembling glass bridge, threatening to sweep you off the narrow span. Below your boots, the deep subterranean shaft drops away into absolute blackness, amplifying the howling wind into a deafening roar. You press yourself low against the vibrating handrails and inch forward while the glass underfoot quivers hard enough to warn you.

The storm is breaking through the upper grates, leaving you precious few moments to reach solid ground on the other side.

nodes.brief: a scene in The Rain Vault: beneath Prism: the seed halls, the lock, every old promise coming due, and the final choice about the seed

exits.label: Descend by the lift shaft
Inspect the weeping stone basin

nodes.title: The Dynamo's Pulse
nodes.page: Thick cables pulse with residual current beside the lift-shaft dynamo, casting long jittery shadows across the concrete floor. The mechanical lift cage sits stranded halfway up its rusted tracks, groaning as the rising wind pressures push against the outer intake shafts. Your ember-lamp flickers in the draft, casting a warm amber glow over the control levers and warning plates.

nodes.brief: a scene in The Rain Vault: beneath Prism: the seed halls, the lock, every old promise coming due, and the final choice about the seed

exits.label: Follow the lift shaft shadows
Inspect the weeping stone basin
Enter the narrow acoustic service tunnel

nodes.title: The Weeping Alcove
nodes.page:
Water slowly trickles from the carved stone eyes of ancient bas-reliefs, filling a shallow marble basin that has remained undisturbed for centuries. The steady, rhythmic plink of droplets provides the only sound in the damp alcove, washing over the lingering scent of salt and stagnant air. Your boots leave wet prints on the stone flags as you approach the edge of the pooling water to examine what lies submerged within.

The vaulted ceiling stretches into darkness above you, hiding several possible exits from the weeping chamber.

nodes.brief: a scene in The Rain Vault: beneath Prism: the seed halls, the lock, every old promise coming due, and the final choice about the seed

exits.label: Press your palm to the biometric scanner
Cross the narrow pit on the rope bridge
Step into the great balance chamber

nodes.title: The Deep Vault Threshold
nodes.page:
Cool air rushes from the dark threshold ahead, carrying the scent of damp earth and unspooling time from the innermost heart of the Seed Vault. Every old promise made by the lensfolk now comes due, hanging heavy in the stillness as your ember-lamp illuminates the massive brass hinges of the inner door. The basin's fate, and the survival of Candlemere's fields, rests entirely on the choice you are about to make.

You stand at the precipice of history, needing only to take the final step into the vault's core.

nodes.brief: a scene in The Rain Vault: beneath Prism: the seed halls, the lock, every old promise coming due, and the final choice about the seed

exits.label: Press your palm against the scanner plate
Cross the narrow span toward the inner sanctum
Turn back to the weeping alcove

nodes.title: The Vault Lock
nodes.page:
Heavy iron gears groan behind the damp stone walls of the Rain Vault, exhaling a breath of ancient ozone and dry dust. The cold ceramic Seedkey rests in your palm, its weight a stark reminder of Candlemere's parched wells and dying lamp-fires. Every old promise made by the lensfolk now converges on this subterranean threshold, demanding an accounting of your journey across the saltglass basin.

Before you lie three distinct paths into the heart of the dormant machinery, each promising a different reckoning with the vault's automated sentinels and silent seed halls.

nodes.brief: a scene in The Rain Vault: beneath Prism: the seed halls, the lock, every old promise coming due, and the final choice about the seed

exits.label: Cross the narrow iron rib above the pit

exits.privWhy: the reader carries the glass-burn scar that marks them as one who crossed the Storm
exits.label: Press your glass-burn scar to the security reader

nodes.title: The Chasm Threshold
nodes.page:
Across the threshold of the innermost sanctum, the floor drops away into a sheer subterranean pit crossed only by a narrow rib of rusted iron. Below, the dark silence of the basin's deep foundation hums with the memory of rushing monsoon waters long overdue. Your banked coal-lantern casts a flickering, warm glow against the towering walls of fused glass and limestone blocks.

Across the dizzying abyss one path uses the suspended rib and a firm nerve; the other calls on old, painful scars earned in the storm.

nodes.brief: a scene in The Rain Vault: beneath Prism: the seed halls, the lock, every old promise coming due, and the final choice about the seed

exits.privWhy: the reader carries the glass-burn scar that marks them as one who crossed the Storm
exits.label: Offer your glass-burn scar to the resting sensor
Step onto the heavy iron weighing pan

nodes.title: The Great Balance
nodes.page:
Inside the chamber of the great balance, a pair of iron pans hang still in the air, waiting for a definitive load to tip their ancient scale. Sulfur and cold copper season the air, along with dust of centuries that have forgotten the sound of rain. Your fingers brush the rough texture of the Seedkey as you weigh the future of Candlemere against the hidden mechanisms of the Old Lensfolk.

The bronze indicator needle shivers against its glass housing, pointing toward the final arbitraments of the vault.

nodes.brief: a scene in The Rain Vault: beneath Prism: the seed halls, the lock, every old promise coming due, and the final choice about the seed

exits.label: Heave harder against the rusted winch
Step into the twilight glare of the core hum

nodes.title: The Sub-Vault Lintel
nodes.page:
Under the low-hanging basalt lintel of the sub-vault, your shoulders ache as you heave against a rusted bronze winch that refuses to yield easily. Phosphor-lamps overhead sputter and fade, casting long, jittery shadows across rows of hermetically sealed tin canisters containing the last drought-proof harvests of the basin. Every movement echoes in the confined space, a reminder of the twenty days remaining before the torrential monsoon floods the lowlands.

Two distinct mechanisms beckon from the gloom, each demanding physical effort or a steady hand on the controls.

nodes.brief: Inside the central control panopticon, banks of dead indicator lights gaze down upon you like the blind eyes of ancient stone deities.

exits.label: Crawl beneath the low basalt lintel

nodes.title: The Blind Panopticon
nodes.page:
Inside the central control panopticon, banks of dead indicator lights gaze down upon you like the blind eyes of ancient stone deities carved by forgotten hands. Dust motes dance lazily in the weak, amber beam of your coal-lantern, illuminating rusted toggle switches and cracked glass dials that have not moved since the old world shattered. The silence here is absolute, broken only by the distant, rhythmic dripping of subterranean moisture somewhere in the dark foundations.

A single egress leads forward into the damp, shadowed machinery of the sub-vault.

nodes.brief: Within the vault's deep refrigeration tier, frost clings to your eyelashes while you calculate the exact temperature needed to preserve the harvest.

exits.label: Wrestle the rusted winch in the sub-vault
Approach the humming core of phosphor-lamps
Seek shelter in the dry innermost reliquary

nodes.title: The Refrigeration Tier
nodes.page:
Frost clings stubbornly to your eyelashes while you calculate the exact temperature needed to preserve the vital seed harvest against the coming heat. Coils of blackened copper snake across the vaulted ceiling, radiating a deep, penetrating chill that bites through your runner's coat. The air is remarkably thin and sharp, carrying the faint, sweet scent of dormant wheat and ancient loam preserved in perpetual winter.

Three separate passages branch outward from this freezing chamber into the humming heart of the installation.

nodes.brief: Beside a heap of shattered quartz lenses, an old automated chime tolls a single mournful note every time the tectonic plates shift below.

exits.label: Pull against the heavy winch in the sub-vault
Investigate the humming phosphor-lamp core

nodes.title: The Quartz Chime
nodes.page:
Beside a heap of shattered quartz lenses, an old automated chime tolls a single mournful note every time the tectonic plates shift deep below the basin. The note travels through the floorboards and up through the soles of your boots with a strange, musical melancholy. Shards of colored glass catch the amber light of your lantern, scattering tiny constellations across the damp stone walls.

Two passages open up from this resonant alcove, leading deeper into the subterranean labyrinth.

nodes.brief: In the sunken gallery where the air tastes of sulfur and old dust, your trembling hand traces the groove of an uncast bronze seal.

exits.label: Approach the humming core of phosphor-lamps
Descend toward the deep drainage sump
Enter the dry and stretched innermost reliquary

nodes.title: The Bronze Seal
nodes.page:
In the sunken gallery where the air tastes distinctly of sulfur and old dust, your trembling hand traces the deep groove of an uncast bronze seal. The metal is freezing to the touch, cut with bas-reliefs of stylized rain clouds and weeping willow boughs that mark the lost harvests of the Old Lensfolk. Your lantern oil is slowly running low, casting flickering boundaries that press closer with every passing minute.

Three distinct routes diverge from the gallery, leading toward the core, the drainage sump, and the dry reliquary.

nodes.brief: Under the massive vaulted ceiling of fused green glass, a network of copper veins pulses faintly with the residual thermal energy of the desert.

exits.label: Follow the cold air toward the deep sump
Push into the bone-dry innermost reliquary
Trace the damp trail across the central hall

nodes.title: The Fused Glass Ceiling
nodes.page:
Under the massive vaulted ceiling of fused green glass, a network of copper veins pulses faintly with the residual thermal energy captured from the desert sun above. The translucent green overhead casts an eerie, submarine glow over your skin and the salt-crusted stone flags underfoot. A low, continuous hum vibrates through the air, sounding like a swarm of giant insects slumbering within the masonry.

Three paths lead onward across the glistening floor toward the deeper vaults and drainage channels.

nodes.brief: Before the sealed titanium bulkhead of the primary seed repository, a row of manual override cranks waits for someone strong enough to turn them.

exits.label: Head toward the rushing air of the sump
Step into the dry silence of the reliquary

nodes.title: The Titanium Bulkhead
nodes.page:
Before the sealed titanium bulkhead of the primary seed repository, a row of manual override cranks waits for someone strong enough to turn them against centuries of accumulated grime. The heavy metal surface is scored with ancient scratch marks, telling silent stories of past runners who fought to reach the grain before the monsoon closed the basin. Your breath fogs slightly in the drafty corridor as you grip the cold iron handles.

Two passages offer a way forward into the chilling depths of the seed vaults.

nodes.brief: Within the shadow of the great condensing tower, droplets of pure water gather on your coat as the subterranean humidity climbs rapidly.

exits.label: Crawl through the damp archway
Follow the cold air toward the sumps
Take the dry passage to the right

nodes.title: The Condensing Tower
nodes.page:
Under the towering shadow of the great condensing tower, droplets of pure water gather thick on your woolen coat as the subterranean humidity climbs rapidly. The air tastes of cold iron and stagnant centuries, heavy with the breath of hidden pipes. Your ember-lamp sputters in the dampness, its banked coals casting a weak orange halo against the weeping stone walls. You stand at a three-way junction where the dripping masonry gives way to echoing drops and distant mechanical groans.

Ahead lies a low service archway choked with condensation, while a sharp draft signals a sudden drop toward the lower drainage sumps to your left, and a thin thread of dry air beckons down a narrow tunnel to your right.

nodes.brief: Across the floor of polished obsidian, a trail of dried white salt crystals marks the path taken by the previous generation's doomed runner.

exits.label: Follow the salt trail toward the grand console
Turn away toward the central hall

nodes.title: The Salt-Scratched Path
nodes.page:
Across the floor of polished obsidian, a trail of dried white salt crystals marks the path taken by the previous generation's doomed runner. Their final journey left a crusty scar across the dark glass, fading into the gloom near a pair of branching archways. Your boots crunch softly over the mineral remnants, and your hand instinctively brushes against the cold ceramic key in your pocket as you study the floor.

The obsidian reflects the dull amber glow of your lantern, magnifying every shadow into a lurking shape. One route leads deeper into the freezing machinery of the vault, while another curves back toward the central hall's salt-encrusted expanses.

nodes.brief: Beside the humming dynamo of the lift shaft, a discarded oil lamp flickers out, plunging you into absolute darkness save for your own coals.

exits.label: Seek the innermost reliquary in the silence
Approach the grand obsidian console ahead
Listen to the singing glass in the hollow pillar

nodes.title: The Dead Lamp
nodes.page:
Next to the lift-shaft dynamo a discarded oil lamp dies, and absolute darkness takes you except for your own coals. Machinery under the floorboards shakes your boots and ribs, drowning every other sound in the subterranean shaft. You lift your ember-lamp higher, watching the weak red glow struggle against the ancient iron bulkheads and grease-stained walls.

From the shadows of the lift machinery three routes peel away, each a different escape from the suffocating gloom of the bay.

nodes.brief: In the alcove of the weeping statues, water slowly trickles from carved stone eyes into a basin that has remained dry for a hundred years.

exits.label: Proceed toward the dry reliquary
Head for the grand obsidian console
Return toward the central hall's salt floor

nodes.title: The Weeping Statues
nodes.page:
In the alcove of the weeping statues, water slowly trickles from carved stone eyes into a basin that has remained dry for a hundred years. The rhythmic plink of droplets echoes hollowly off the vaulted ceiling, breaking the heavy silence of the sealed vault. Your coat feels damp against your shoulders, and the smell of ancient mineral dust fills your nose as you pause before the stone figures.

Behind the weeping alcove, three paths branch out into the darkness: one leads toward the deep reliquary, another toward the obsidian console, and the third winds back across the salt floor.

nodes.brief: Within the narrow service tunnel lined with acoustic tiles, every breath sounds like a thunderclap against the silence of the dead city.

exits.label: Follow the quiet hum toward the reliquary
Turn toward the hum of the obsidian console
Backtrack toward the central hall's damp trail

nodes.title: The Acoustic Tunnel
nodes.page:
Within the narrow service tunnel lined with acoustic tiles, every breath sounds like a thunderclap against the silence of the dead city. The perforated metal walls trap your whispers and bounce them back as a distorted chorus, making your own movements feel unnervingly public. Your ember-lamp casts long, jittery shadows ahead of your boots as you navigate the claustrophobic conduit.

The passage opens up shortly into three distinct directions, each carrying its own faint acoustic signature from the depths of the complex.

nodes.brief: Before the secondary biometric scanner, your bare palm presses against the cold metal plate while the system checks your lineage for authority.

exits.label: Step forward to the grand obsidian console
Enter the hollow pillar of singing glass

nodes.title: The Biometric Scanner
nodes.page:
Before the secondary biometric scanner, your bare palm presses against the cold metal plate while the system checks your lineage for authority. The metal bites into your skin with an icy nip, and a faint blue luminescence washes over your knuckles as internal cogs click into place. Your breath catches in your throat as you wait for the ancient machinery to either accept your bloodline or sound a harsh alarm.

When the green status light finally flickers on, two separate pathways unlock within the recessed wall before you.

nodes.brief: Across the threshold of the innermost sanctum, the floor drops away into a sheer pit crossed only by a narrow rail of wrought iron.

exits.label: Cross toward the singing glass pillar
Make your way to the final titanium door
Take the reckless way

nodes.title: The Iron Rail
nodes.page: Across the threshold of the innermost sanctum, the floor drops away into a sheer pit crossed only by a narrow rail of wrought iron. The drop below is swallowed by absolute blackness, save for the faint red embers of your lantern reflecting off the polished metal bar. The wind howls upward from the chasm with a dry, melodic whistle that rattles the teeth in your jaw.

nodes.brief: Because the jagged glass-burn scar across your forearm matches the old protocol, the automated defense turret retracts into the ribbed ceiling.

exits.label: Approach the final titanium door

priv.why: the reader carries the glass-burn scar that marks them as one who crossed the Storm

nodes.title: The Burn Scar
nodes.page:
Because the jagged glass-burn scar across your forearm matches the old protocol, the automated defense turret retracts silently into the ribbed ceiling. The puckered pink skin throbs faintly as if remembering the searing desert storm that carved it into your flesh years ago. A soft pneumatic hiss greets your approach as the heavy machinery recognizes one who survived the glass-wastes.

The pathway ahead stands clear, inviting you to take the final steps toward the ultimate door of the seed repository.

nodes.brief: Within the chamber of the great balance, two heavy iron pans hang suspended in stillness, waiting for you to place the seed upon them.

exits.label: Retrace your steps to the central hall
Carry the seed to the titanium door

nodes.title: The Great Balance
nodes.page: Within the chamber of the great balance, two heavy iron pans hang suspended in stillness, waiting for you to place the seed upon them. The massive brass arms gleam under your lantern light, balanced on a knife-edge that has not tipped for generations. The air here is perfectly dead, smelling of old iron and dried desert blooms preserved in amber silence.

nodes.brief: Under the low-hanging basalt lintel of the sub-vault, your shoulders ache as you heave against the rusted winch of the floodgate.

exits.label: Climb toward the central platform

nodes.title: The Basalt Lintel
nodes.page:
Under the low-hanging basalt lintel of the sub-vault, your shoulders ache as you heave against the rusted winch of the floodgate. Red flakes of ancient scale peel away under your grip, falling into the dark bilge water below with a dull splash. Your ember-lamp swings wildly from your wrist, casting frantic arcs of orange light across the slick, sweating stone walls.

With a final wrenching groan the iron mechanism gives way and frees the path upward to the apex of the central vault platform.

nodes.brief: In the twilight glare of phosphor-lamps, the core of the seed vault hums with a restrained, terrifying potential energy.

exits.label: Touch the trembling copper plate to release the stored charge
Step back from the humming core and test the latch on the secondary case

nodes.title: Phosphor Glare and Hum
nodes.page:
Phosphor-lamps hiss along the ribbed ceiling, casting a greenish twilight over the seed vault's thrumming core where restrained energy vibrates against your teeth. Every heavy copper conduit pulses with the strange, low frequency of a sleeping beast, waiting for a touch that might awaken or shatter it.

You stand with the ceramic key growing warm in your damp palm, feeling the steady tremor of the bedrock beneath your boots. Every breath tastes of ozone and dry limestone, urging a decision before the subterranean silence breaks entirely.

nodes.brief: Beside the deep sump where the basin's drainage channels converge, a sudden rush of cold air announces the arrival of the monsoon underground.

exits.label: Climb down the iron rungs toward the rising damp
Seal the drainage grate with the heavy iron wedge

nodes.title: Wind from the Sump
nodes.page:
Cold air rushes up from the deep stone sump where the basin's drainage channels converge, carrying the sharp scent of wet mud and distant rain. Below your feet, the first underground stirrings of the monsoon echo through the dark tunnels like a gathering crowd.

Shadows stretch long across the algae-slicked masonry as the draft grows stronger, fluttering the edges of your coat and chilling the sweat on the back of your neck. The water is rising faster than the old ledgers predicted, turning every calculation into a race against the rising tide.

nodes.brief: Within the vault's innermost reliquary, the air is so dry and still that your skin feels tight and stretched like parchment.

exits.label: Uncork the central jar to test the ancient seed
Leave the reliquary untouched and check the heavy outer latch
Turn your back on the quiet shelves and retrace your steps

nodes.title: Parchment Air of Relics
nodes.page:
Dry stillness fills the innermost reliquary, pulling the moisture from your skin until your knuckles feel tight and stretched like yellow parchment. Rows of glass jars, housing dust-fine grains and shrivelled pods, line the cedar shelves under a fine blanket of unblemished salt.

Silence presses down with physical weight, broken only by the faint crackle of your banked coal-lantern shifting against your hip. The air holds no scent of life, only the mineral breath of centuries past preserved in amber glass.

nodes.brief: Before the grand obsidian console, three separate slots wait for decisions that will shape the survival or doom of every western lamp-town.

exits.label: Press the left slot to open the deep irrigation sluices
Slide the cold key into the central locking channel

nodes.title: The Grand Obsidian Console
nodes.page:
Three obsidian slots wait upon the polished console for choices that will shape the survival or doom of every western lamp-town. The smooth volcanic glass reflects the dim orange glow of your coal-lantern, looking like dark pools waiting for a heavy stone to drop.

Your fingers hover above the cold stone plates, each indentation carved with the jagged runic script of the old lensfolk. The responsibility of an entire harvest hangs upon which groove receives your pressure first.

nodes.brief: Across the glistening salt-encrusted floor of the central hall, your footprints leave a dark, damp trail that stands out starkly against the white crust.

exits.label: Follow the damp trail toward the echoing water-conduit
Veer toward the obsidian console to lock the central sector

nodes.title: Damp Trail on Salt
nodes.page:
Dark footprints mar the glistening white crust of the central hall, standing out like ink spilled across a clean linen sheet. The salt floor crunches softly under your boots, leaving wet rings that slowly fill with bitter brine seeping up from below.

Across the vast chamber, the dim green glow of the ceiling lamps flickers erratically, throwing long and dancing shadows against the carved pillars. You are leaving a clear path behind you, one that anyone or anything could easily follow into the dark.

nodes.brief: Within the hollow pillar of singing glass, your name is whispered back to you by unseen acoustic chambers buried deep in the bedrock.

exits.label: Leave the singing chamber before the echoes grow too loud

nodes.title: Hollow Pillar of Singing Glass
nodes.page:
Acoustic chambers buried deep in the bedrock catch your voice and bounce your name back through the hollow pillar of singing glass like a choir of strangers. The tone shifts from a low, resonant hum to a bright, piercing chime that sets your teeth on edge.

Vibrations travel up through the stone floor, making the salt crystals on the walls dance in shimmering patterns of grey and silver. The glass pillar seems to listen, recording every whispered word into the ancient memory of the basin.

nodes.brief: Beside the final heavy titanium door of the seed repository, the cold ceramic key grows warm in your fist as if anticipating the latch.

exits.label: Insert the warm key into the heavy titanium door

nodes.title: Warmth of the Key
nodes.page:
Heavy titanium doors block the entrance to the seed repository, their massive bolts chilled by centuries of subterranean frost. Yet as you approach, the cold ceramic key in your fist grows strangely warm, pulsing with an inner heat that matches the beat of your heart.

Frost crystals melt into tiny droplets where your fingers press against the porous clay, releasing a scent like wet dust after a long drought. The lock mechanism waits, a silent mouth carved into the metal waiting for its missing tooth.

nodes.brief: At the apex of the central vault platform, the great seed-urn opens its iron petals to reveal the pale, dormant grains of the old world.

exits.label: Press on into the heart of the vault

nodes.title: Iron Petals of the Urn
nodes.page:
Iron petals part with a slow, grinding screech at the apex of the central platform, revealing the pale, dormant grains of the old world resting upon a velvet cushion of woven copper wire. A faint cloud of dry, golden dust rises from the opening, smelling faintly of old flour and crushed stones.

You lean over the rim, holding your breath as the lantern light washes across the tiny, perfect shapes of seeds that have not seen rain or sun in a thousand years. The future of Candlemere rests in the hollow of your hand, waiting to be claimed or left to dust.

nodes.brief: Before the yawning breach of the water-conduit, you must choose whether to flood the basin now and save the crops or preserve the dry vault.

exits.label: Press on through the roaring spray
Turn back before the rising water cuts off your escape

nodes.title: Breach of the Conduit
nodes.page:
Yawning stonework marks the breach of the water-conduit, where a torrent of dark, foaming brine surges against the rusted grating with the force of a battering ram. The roar of water fills the low tunnel, drowning out all other sound and sending cold spray misting across your face.

You must choose whether to break the remaining bars and flood the basin now to save the parched fields above, or shore up the dry vault to keep the ancient seeds safe from the tide. Every second brings a new shudder to the straining masonry around you.

nodes.brief: Overlooking the vast submerged expanse of the saltglass sea from the high observatory balcony, you hold the destiny of Candlemere in your palm.

exits.label: Press on toward the final platform

nodes.title: High Observatory Balcony
nodes.page:
High observatory arches frame the vast submerged expanse of the saltglass sea, where distant lightning flickers across the grey belly of storm clouds gathering over the horizon. From this dizzying height, the shattered glass cities look like broken teeth jutting from a mirror of salt.

The wind pulls at your cloak, bringing the sharp tang of approaching rain and the distant, haunting whistle of wind through the spires. You hold the destiny of Candlemere in your palm, looking out over a world about to be drowned or washed clean.

nodes.brief: In the quiet stillness after the vault mechanism locks into place, you face the long walk back into a world transformed by water and salt.

exits.label: Step through the arch and press on across the rising waters

nodes.title: The Vault Lock Settles
nodes.page:
Heavy iron pins drop home within the cooled housing with a sound like dropped gravel, ending generations of waiting. Silence returns to the high circular gallery, save for the wet hiss of condensation weeping down walls of fused crystal. Your fingers still ache from the leverage of the cold ceramic key, yet the air around you tastes startlingly sweet, smelling faintly of damp loam and unopened leaves. Outside the narrow viewing slit, grey storm light churns across the flooded flats of the Salt Basin, where the rising monsoon laps hungrily at the lower lintels.

The long road back begins here, leading across waters that have swallowed the tracks of your arrival and transformed every familiar salt-arch into a strange grey harbor.

nodes.brief: Ignoring all structural warnings, you recklessly jam the Seedkey into a rusted pressure valve, triggering a catastrophic collapse that seals your doom forever.
nodes.title: The Rusted Valve
nodes.page: Ignoring all structural warnings, you recklessly jam the Seedkey into a rusted pressure valve, triggering a catastrophic collapse that seals your doom forever. A deafening shriek of shearing metal echoes through the chamber as the ancient stone lintels fracture overhead. Tons of glittering salt and shattered glass cascade down from the low ceiling, burying the lantern light and ending your journey in the silent heart of the basin.

nodes.brief: Rushing blindly past the warning chimes, you force the main lock without setting the pressure release, sealing yourself forever inside the collapsing vault.
nodes.title: The Sealed Chamber
nodes.page: Warning bells clang once through the conduit before the pressure lock seizes with a shriek of tortured brass. Frantic fingers slip against the smooth ceramic key as the heavy lead-lined bolts slide home from the outside, locking forever into wet stone. Dark, foaming brine surges over the threshold in a sudden, cold wave, filling the narrow alcove and driving the air from your lungs with astonishing speed. The ember-lamp hisses and dies in the rising dark, leaving only the distant, hollow echo of water finding its final, quiet level.

nodes.brief: The reader has chosen to open the rain vault to everyone: the moment of carrying it out, with the consequences about to fall (do not decide which of the endings it is; the exits do that).

exits.label: Watch the seed wake across the waters
Step back as the unthanked doors swing wide
Turn away before the waiting crowd arrives

nodes.title: Opening the Great Doors
nodes.page:
Trembling hands guide the cold ceramic key through the bronze wards until the entire locking assembly gives way with a deep metallic note. Singing glass chimes ring out from the high ceiling as the great valves swing wide, releasing a cool, sweet draft of long-hoarded mountain air into the salt-fogged hall. The Sisters' well-song rises from somewhere deep within the descending conduits, blending with the roar of the rising monsoon to herald an end to the long drought.

Down every flooded corridor and up through the shattered lens-cities, the water begins to flow outward, carrying the promise of green harvests to every throat that ever cried for rain.

nodes.brief: The reader has chosen to seal the vault and guard its secret: the moment of carrying it out, with the consequences about to fall (do not decide which of the endings it is; the exits do that).

exits.label: Leave the door in the hands of Calder
Turn away and leave the vault to the glass

nodes.title: Sealing the Vault
nodes.page:
Heavy lead bars drop into their greased channels with a final, flat thud that vibrates through the soles of your boots. The bronze door grinds shut against its stone frame, sealing the ancient seed away from the desperate hands of the Salt Court and the thirsty pilgrims alike. Outside the high balcony, grey rain drives across the glass sea, but within this chamber, the secret remains intact and untouched by the rising tide.

The key slides deep into a crevice of living rock, leaving the vault to the silence of the drowned city and the watchful care of the deep stone.

nodes.brief: The reader has chosen to take only the seed and run for candlemere: the moment of carrying it out, with the consequences about to fall (do not decide which of the endings it is; the exits do that).

exits.label: Head for home with a clean pack
Step into the storm with the Salt Court debt behind you
Walk out into the dark road without a light

nodes.title: Taking the Seed
nodes.page:
Quick fingers lift the primary seed-pod from its silver cradle and tuck the cold treasure deep into the folds of your travel coat. The great doors behind you remain half-shut, ignoring the rising flood and the distant calls of the Basin's many factions. Every step toward the exit carries what you leave behind, yet the small hard shape against your ribs promises life for the hearths of home.

The path out leads through the rising brine and back toward the western rim, owing nothing to the court lords or the singing sisters.

nodes.brief: Ending "The Seed Wakes": You open the Rain Vault to everyone: the key turns clean and the Sisters' well-song carries; the seed goes out along every road and Candlemere is fed.

exits.label: Read on to the final moment

nodes.title: The Seed Wakes
nodes.page:
Sweet water surges through the old stone arteries of the Basin, carrying the first sprouting grains out upon the surface of the rising flood. The Sisters' well-song echoes from every submerged tower, matching the drumming rhythm of the monsoon rain. Down in Candlemere, the dry mud of the marketplace drinks deeply, and green shoots push through the crust before the month is half gone.

Your fingers no longer ache from the key, but the memory of the cold ceramic stays with you as proof that old promises can still be kept.

nodes.brief: Aftermath of "The Seed Wakes": what changes for the people of the Basin and Candlemere, weeks later.

exits.label: Reach the last page of the journey

nodes.title: Green Valleys
nodes.page:
Weeks after the gates swung wide, the salt flats are a shimmering expanse of shallow freshwater where flat-bottomed skiffs pole between drowned glass spires. No one starves this season, and the lamps of Candlemere burn bright with oil pressed from the very first riverside harvest. The Salt Court finds its promissory notes dissolved in the rising tide, replaced by a strange, unaccustomed equity among neighbors.

Even the Dune Sisters offer a cup of fresh well-water without asking for an oath in return, smiling wryly as the rain drums on their broad straw hats.

nodes.brief: Final page of "The Seed Wakes": a closing image and a last line for the book.
nodes.title: The Last Lamp
nodes.page:
The ember-lamp sits unlit on the wooden table, its banked coals grown cold in a house that no longer fears the dark or the drought. Outside the window, the young grain grows tall and green beneath a grey, forgiving sky that smells forever of wet earth and salt-free wind. You walk down to the water's edge where the small boats tie up, watching the ripples spread outward toward the horizon where the old world ended and the new one finally took root.

The lamp is out, but the road goes on.

nodes.brief: Ending "Opened, Unthanked": You open the vault to everyone and it works, but nobody sang for you and the Sisters and the Salt Court both claim the seed; you walk home with a clean key and a hard peace.

exits.label: Read on through the quiet aftermath

nodes.title: Opened, Unthanked
nodes.page:
The heavy doors yield to the cold key just as the old songs promised, flooding the Basin with the rich, damp scent of life-giving water. Yet no crowd gathers to cheer your name, and neither the Sisters nor the Salt Court acknowledge the hand that turned the lock. The seed is loose upon the waters, flowing toward every thirsty field from Prism to the western rim without a single word of gratitude.

You walk back along the flooded causeway alone, your pockets empty of coin but your pack light with the quiet satisfaction of a hard task finished.

nodes.brief: Aftermath of "Opened, Unthanked": what changes for the people of the Basin and Candlemere, weeks later.

exits.label: Read the final lines of the road

nodes.title: The Hard Peace
nodes.page:
Months pass under a grey, dripping sky, and the Basin thrives despite the silence left in your wake. The harvest rises green and high across the flats, feeding every town and homestead while the great factions argue over who deserves the credit for the rain. Nobody remembers the runner from Candlemere who turned the key in the dark, and your name is written on no monument in the glass cities.

Yet the wells run full when you pass them, and the salt on your boots has washed away into rich, dark mud that clings to the roots of new trees.

nodes.brief: Final page of "Opened, Unthanked": a closing image and a last line for the book.
nodes.title: Unsung Roads
nodes.page:
The ember-lamp burns low on the sill and lays warm light across a kitchen table laden with bread from the new harvest. You watch the rain stitch silver lines across the glass panes, listening to the contented murmur of a town that no longer looks toward the desert with dread. There are no songs sung about your journey, and no statues stand in the drowned squares to mark your passing.

The seed is in the earth where it belongs, and the road ahead is wide, quiet, and entirely your own.

nodes.brief: Ending "The Door That Stuck": You open the vault, but the cracked key fails halfway; the door opens a hand's width and then freezes, and the seed spills out in a crush of hands.

exits.label: Turn the page and read on

nodes.title: The Door That Stuck
nodes.page: Cold ceramic bites your palm as you force the Seedkey into the rusted tumbler of the Rain Vault, but the ancient mechanism shudders and binds tight at the half-turn. A sharp crack echoes through the cavernous gloom, and the heavy iron doors grind to a stubborn halt, leaving only a narrow hand-width of darkness between the leaves. Before you can wedge a shoulder against the metal, a surge of frantic movement erupts from the shadows as desperate hands reach through the gap, clawing eagerly at the spilling cascade of ancient, dormant grain that pours out in a golden, crushing wave.

nodes.brief: Aftermath of "The Door That Stuck": what changes for the people of the Basin and Candlemere, weeks later.

exits.label: Turn forward to the last page

nodes.title: The Door That Stuck
nodes.page: Grey rain keeps falling for months on end, and the Basin still feeds itself while nobody marks the runner who cracked the vault. The spilled seed takes root in the wet silt washed down by the early monsoon, turning the cracked salt crust into a sprawling green patchwork of stubborn life. Candlemere fills its granaries with the unexpected harvest, though the giant doors of Prism remain forever wedged, a rusted monument to a clumsy rescue. People speak of the runner who cracked the vault with a wry shake of the head, grateful for the heavy bread on their tables even if the great hall stayed locked.

nodes.brief: Final page of "The Door That Stuck": a closing image and a last line for the book.
nodes.title: The Door That Stuck
nodes.page: An ember-lamp gutters on the sill, throwing amber light over a kitchen table stacked with bread from the new harvest. Outside, the rain taps a gentle, endless rhythm against the glass, washing away the last white traces of the salt flats from your worn boots. You sit by the hearth with your hands empty of keys and heavy with rest, listening to the soft murmur of a valley that has finally learned how to drink. The salt has gone back to the sea, the lenses are cool and dark in the observatory above, and the lamp needs no more oil than what remains in the wick.

nodes.brief: Ending "Calder Keeps the Door": You seal the Rain Vault to keep the seed safe; Calder stays as its keeper and you walk home lighter, with a friend's promise to wait.

exits.label: Turn the page and read on

nodes.title: Calder Keeps the Door
nodes.page: Metal clicks against stone as you drive the bolt home, sealing the Rain Vault before the rising damp can spoil the harvest within. Calder leans against the archway with a faint, wry smile, hitching a leather pack and offering to watch the threshold while the world dries out. You leave the cold ceramic key in trusted hands, knowing the seed is safe behind glass and steel until the drought returns. Walking out into the salt-scoured air feels remarkably different when you carry no debt upon your shoulders and a good friend keeps watch behind you.

nodes.brief: Aftermath of "Calder Keeps the Door": what changes for the people of the Basin and Candlemere, weeks later.

exits.label: Turn forward to the last page

nodes.title: The Door That Stuck
nodes.page: Grey months crawl past under a dripping sky, and the Basin keeps its green while you walk roads that no longer need a runner. Word filters back from the center of the dried sea that Calder keeps the great doors well, trading signals with the glass-sentries through flashes of polished mirror. Candlemere receives its share of the sealed grain by swift runner-post, and the villagers speak warmly of the diver who stayed behind in the dark. The wells run full and clear from the rim to the observatory, proving that some treasures are better guarded by a steadfast friend than an army of toll-lords.

nodes.brief: Final page of "Calder Keeps the Door": a closing image and a last line for the book.
nodes.title: Calder Keeps the Door
nodes.page: On the sill an oil lamp burns down to a stub, lighting a kitchen table that holds fresh bread from the new harvest. Outside, the rain taps a gentle, endless rhythm against the glass, washing away the last white traces of the salt flats from your worn boots. You pour two cups of hot chicory, leaving one cold spot on the wood for a friend who is still down in the dark keeping watch over the world's bread. The basin outside is a lake of silver water now, and the lamps of Candlemere burn bright and untroubled against the coming night.

nodes.brief: Ending "The Vault Remembers": You seal the vault alone and leave it to the glass; the seed is safe, but nobody remembers where the door is and the years go by.

exits.label: Turn the page and read on

nodes.title: The Vault Remembers
nodes.page: In the gloom, iron hinges groan as you turn the Seedkey twice and throw the ancient latches, locking the Rain Vault away from a world too eager to spend its future. You leave the door shrouded in shadows and sealed with a touch of mirror-glass, and the desert takes back the secret threshold beneath Prism. Nobody watches the entrance now, and the paths leading inward fade beneath the drifting salt storms until even the sharpest-eyed glass-diver would fail to spot the seam. You walk away into the shimmering glare with an empty palm and a quiet conscience.

nodes.brief: Aftermath of "The Vault Remembers": what changes for the people of the Basin and Candlemere, weeks later.

exits.label: Turn forward to the last page

nodes.title: The Door That Stuck
nodes.page: Under a dripping grey sky the months stack up, and the Basin drinks its fill while the vault you sealed stays lost to every map. The great monsoon arrives on schedule, filling the dry lakebeds with sweet grey water while the secret vault remains hidden beneath the rising tides. People in Candlemere nibble on hard-won bread and wonder where the old legends went, forgetting the exact location of the door that saved them without ever opening. The desert remembers what the living lose, folding its treasures deep beneath the glass crust where no toll-lord or runner can ever touch them again.

nodes.brief: Final page of "The Vault Remembers": a closing image and a last line for the book.
nodes.title: The Vault Remembers
nodes.page: A single lamp on the sill throws a soft circle of light across a kitchen table set with bread from the new harvest. Outside, the rain taps a gentle, endless rhythm against the glass, washing away the last white traces of the salt flats from your worn boots. You sit alone in the quiet kitchen, listening to the water rise against the doorframes of a town that no longer needs to run across the dried sea. The key is gone, the vault is silent, and the lamp rests happily in the dark.

nodes.brief: Ending "Clean Hands, Heavy Pack": You take only the seed and run for Candlemere, owing nobody; the road is long but yours, and the fields green at the rim.

exits.label: Turn the page and read on

nodes.title: Clean Hands, Heavy Pack
nodes.page: Cold ceramic slides back into your leather pouch as you snatch a handful of prime seed from the open bin, leaving the rest untouched for the hills to claim. You turn your back on the glittering machinery of Prism before the salt-guards can notice the theft or the toll-lords can write a new contract in blood. The road back to the western rim is long and steep, but your pack is heavy with honest grain and your debts are paid to nobody. Every step northward brings the smell of damp earth closer, drowning out the bitter tang of the glass sea.

nodes.brief: Aftermath of "Clean Hands, Heavy Pack": what changes for the people of the Basin and Candlemere, weeks later.

exits.label: Turn forward to the last page

nodes.title: The Door That Stuck
nodes.page: Month after month the grey sky drips on, and Candlemere thickens with the seed you took while the Basin forgets who carried it. The stolen seed sprouts vigorously in the garden plots behind Candlemere, yielding tall stalks of golden wheat that defy the old curse of the dry rim. You owe no taxes to the Salt Court and no oaths to the Dune Sisters, walking the village streets as a simple runner who did what needed doing. The town council asks few questions about how the sack was filled, preferring to taste the sweet bread and watch the rain fill the barrels.

nodes.brief: Final page of "Clean Hands, Heavy Pack": a closing image and a last line for the book.
nodes.title: Clean Hands, Heavy Pack
nodes.page: The lamp on the sill is nearly out, and its small circle of light falls on a kitchen table crowded with bread from the new harvest. Outside, the rain taps a gentle, endless rhythm against the glass, washing away the last white traces of the salt flats from your worn boots. You hang your leather running-pack from the rafters for the final time, knowing the long race across the mirror desert is over. The lamps of the town shine steadily in the mist, and the soil outside the door is dark, rich, and deeply wet.

nodes.brief: Ending "Light on the Road": You take the seed and run with the Salt Court's debt on your back; the ember-lamp still burns, and its light makes you a target and a beacon both.

exits.label: Turn the page and read on

nodes.title: Light on the Road
nodes.page:
Cold ceramic bites into your palm as you turn your back on the vault's open maw, the Seedkey heavy and settled in your tunic. Behind you, the Salt Court's ledger-men shout into the whistling wind, their ink-pots frozen and their high-interest tallies reduced to fluttering scraps of paper against the white glare. You carry their crushing debt pinned to your name, yet the ember-lamp still swings from your wrist, its banked coals glowing a stubborn, bruised red through the soot-stained tin. That spark makes you a moving target for every toll-lord between Prism and the western rim, but it also carves a defiant corridor through the encroaching dusk. Every step forward on the salt-crust kicks up fine, glittering dust that catches the coal-light, turning your lonely flight into a procession of one.

You do not look back at the shattered towers or the silent glasswrights watching from their high mirrors, because the horizon ahead belongs entirely to the long, hard miles of your return.

nodes.brief: Aftermath of "Light on the Road": what changes for the people of the Basin and Candlemere, weeks later.

exits.label: Turn to the last page

nodes.title: Light on the Road
nodes.page:
Weeks after your return, the western rim hums with a strange, anxious vitality as sacks of ancient, drought-proof grain are hoisted across thresholds in Candlemere. The fields that once lay cracked and grey now sprout green shoots under a sky thick with the heavy promise of the impending monsoon, proving that the price of the Salt Court's ledger was worth every bitter coin. Creditors ride out from the basin on tall, nervous mounts to peer down village lanes, but they find a community too busy with planting and harvest-prep to offer them more than polite, stony silence. Your ember-lamp, now retired to the mantle of the communal hall, still holds a dull warmth at its core, reminding anyone who enters of the night you brought the future home through the salt-flats. People nod when you pass, their eyes lingering on the debt collectors who pace the perimeter fences like hungry dogs locked out of a warm kitchen.

The ledger-lords hold your name in their ink-books, but the soil holds the seed, and the green shoots care nothing for interest rates.

nodes.brief: Final page of "Light on the Road": a closing image and a last line for the book.
nodes.title: Light on the Road
nodes.page: Night settles over Candlemere like a dropped blanket, quiet and smelling of damp earth and crushed mint from the newly watered ditch-banks. In the centre of the village, the old communal hall stands tall against the stars, its roof patched and ready for the first heavy drops of the Return that will soon soak the entire basin. You sit on the low stone step outside your kitchen door, fingers brushing against the cold, empty shape where the Seedkey once rested before it unlocked the world. Far across the salt-flats, a single mirror-flash from Prism blinks once, twice, three times - a distant, wordless signal from glasswrights who know the cycle has turned and the basin is whole again. You close your eyes against the cool night wind, listening to the steady, collective breathing of a town that has survived the drought. The lamp has gone out at last, its coals turned to grey ash, but the dark no longer feels empty or cold.

nodes.brief: Ending "The Dark Walk Home": You take the seed and walk home in the dark with the Salt Court's debt behind you and no lamp; a long, quiet, uncertain return.

exits.label: Turn the page and read on

nodes.title: The Dark Walk Home
nodes.page:
Fingers trace the cold ceramic of the Seedkey one final time before you pull the heavy bronze doors of the vault shut, leaving the Salt Court's agents howling in the echoing dark behind you. You walk away from Prism with their vast, impossible debt trailing in your wake, carrying the future of the basin in your tunic while you extinguish the ember-lamp completely to save yourself from tracking eyes. Without the coal-lantern's red glow, the night swallows you whole, turning the salt-crust into an endless, grey sea under a starless sky where only the crunch of salt beneath your boots marks your passage. Darkness is absolute, smelling of old dust and the distant rising humidity of the coming monsoon, so you navigate by memory and the slope of the ground alone. It is a lonely, quiet return, stripped of beacons and warnings, leaving you with only the weight of your choices and the chill of the open basin.

Every shadow feels like a toll-lord waiting in the salt-dunes, yet you keep walking through the blackness, invisible and unguided.

nodes.brief: Aftermath of "The Dark Walk Home": what changes for the people of the Basin and Candlemere, weeks later.

exits.label: Turn to the last page

nodes.title: The Dark Walk Home
nodes.page:
Months slip by in a blur of quiet toil, and the grey skies above Candlemere finally break open into the long-awaited rains, feeding the newly sown fields without a single spark of lamp-light to mark your triumph. The villagers whisper of how you returned empty-handed of lanterns but heavy-laden with the seeds of a thousand forgotten harvests, slipping through the cordon of salt-lords like smoke through a wicker hurdle. Creditors still patrol the perimeter roads on moonless nights, checking ledgers by torchlight and demanding interest from doors that remain firmly bolted against them. Yet the crops grow high and green in the valley floor, indifferent to the financial storms brewing beyond the fences, and the people of Candlemere sleep soundly behind walls built on quiet defiance. You walk the muddy lanes in the midday sun without a lamp swinging from your wrist, nodding to neighbors who know the price you paid to keep the town out of the ledger-men's pockets.

The debt remains unpaid in the high ledgers of the basin, but the granaries are full, and no one asks for light in broad daylight.

nodes.brief: Final page of "The Dark Walk Home": a closing image and a last line for the book.
nodes.title: The Dark Walk Home
nodes.page: Rain drums a steady, comforting rhythm against the slate roof of Candlemere, washing the salt-dust from the eaves and soaking deep into the rich earth of the new fields. Inside your kitchen, the hearth fire crackles with dry brushwood, casting dancing orange shadows across the walls where an unlit lantern hangs cold and forgotten from its iron hook. You sit at the wooden table with empty hands, listening to the water gurgle through the street-drains outside as the great basin fills for the first time in a generation. Somewhere out there in the dark and the rising flood, the Salt Court's books sit waterlogged and useless, their ink running red and black into the rising tide. The journey is over, the seed is in the ground, and the long, quiet walk home has brought you to a place where no one asks for tolls or targets. You close your eyes against the firelight, resting easily in the deep, unlit peace of a world beginning anew.
